courses.offered_text: May Term (implied by "Students must enroll during May Term for both INTL 3433 and FINA 3163.").

courses.subject: INTL
courses.subject_name: Daniel and Betty Jo Grant Center for International Education
courses.title: International Studies Seminar
courses.description: This course is designed for students who have completed an overseas study experience. The course will assist in a student's reflection on his or her overseas experience. This course is required for the minor in International Studies and must be taken the semester the student returns from a semester of study abroad. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: INTL
courses.subject_name: Daniel and Betty Jo Grant Center for International Education
courses.title: Second Language Assessment
courses.description: This course acquaints the language teacher with purposes and types of assessments, including self- and peer-assessments, criterion-based assessments and rubrics, and various performance-based assessment tools. Prerequisites: INTL 2043 and INTL 3043. Online Spring 2 term.

courses.subject: INTL
courses.subject_name: Daniel and Betty Jo Grant Center for International Education
courses.title: International Study Abroad
courses.description: One or two semesters of study may be taken at an approved international site. See International Study Program. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: INTL
courses.subject_name: Daniel and Betty Jo Grant Center for International Education
courses.title: International Study Abroad Practicum
courses.description: A course designed to complement the international study abroad experience. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: KIN
courses.title: Concepts of Wellness
courses.description: Students will examine their fitness needs, producing an exercise program and lifetime personal fitness goals. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: KIN
courses.title: Foundations of Kinesiology
courses.description: An introductory course in the disciplines of physical education and sport and for the major/minor. Basic concepts, principles and the changing nature of this multifaceted field will be studied. Prerequisite to all required KIN courses. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: KIN
courses.title: Fundamental Motor Development
courses.description: A systematic study of motor and skill development from childhood through adulthood with special emphasis upon the conditions for effective motor learning. Prerequisite: KIN 1003. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: KIN
courses.title: Outdoor Leisure Pursuits
courses.description: This course is designed to introduce outdoor leisure activities, along with basic skills and techniques needed to continue li fe-long participation leading to the development of a healthier active lifestyle. The student will gain information about outdoor r ecreation resources in the community and learn to make full use of them. Activities which may be incorporated include hiking, geo cachi ng, orienteering, disc spo…
courses.prereq_text: Ability to participate and a demonstrated ability to swim
prereq_other: Ability to participate and a demonstrated ability to swim

courses.subject: KIN
courses.title: Drug Education
courses.description: An exploration of the physical, mental, emotional, and social aspects of drug use and abuse. Special attention will be focused on proper use of drugs in contemporary society. Spring.

courses.subject: KIN
courses.title: Health and Safety
courses.description: A course that deals with the principles of personal health, health risk and appraisal, and interpersonal relationships. Issues in nutrition, exercise, mental health and mental illness, stress, domestic violence and prevention of chronic disease. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: KIN
courses.title: Structural Basis of Human Movement
courses.description: A study of human movement from an anatomical perspective as it applies to physical activity. KIN majors or permission of inst ructor. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: KIN
courses.title: Methods of Strength Training and Conditioning
courses.description: A study of the methodology of teaching various strength and conditioning programs to prepare strength coaches, personal trainers, and health club professionals. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: KIN
courses.title: Care and Prevention of Injuries
courses.description: This course is designed for those seeking admission into a master’s degree program in athletic training, sports medicine, and health care professions. Using outcomes-based curriculum, proven methods of sports injury evaluation, therapy and return to play d ecisions will be addressed. Laboratory times will focus on introducing the clinical skills necessary for admission to the above -mentioned programs. Prerequisites:…

courses.subject: KIN
courses.title: Physiology of Exercise
courses.description: A study of bodily functions under the stress of muscular activity. Prerequisite: KIN 1003, 1113, KIN 2093 or BIOL 2014. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: KIN
courses.title: Program Design and Management
courses.description: This course covers the principles of planning and implementing general exercise programs designed for group involvement. Topi cs include identification of exercise needs, categories of exercise activities, programming formats, and integration of people with disabilities into general exercise programs. Upon completion, students will be able to develop and implement activities based upon partici pants’ needs, interests…

courses.subject: KIN
courses.title: Adapted Kinesiology Methods
courses.description: A course designed to help prepare the exercise-related professional to meet the needs of the disabled in schools and society. Prerequisites: KIN 1003, 1113, 2093. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: KIN
courses.title: Methods of Physical Activity for Children
courses.description: An activity class to give prospective teachers a broad range of developmentally appropriate activities for the different deve lopmental skill levels of elementary age children with implications for physical education, program content, teaching techniques, a nd materials. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: KIN
courses.title: Methods of Teaching and Coaching
courses.description: This course is designed to assist students in becoming skilled and knowledgeable in teaching and coaching individual and team activities. Emphasis will be placed on developing and evaluating the student's skills and knowledge. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: KIN
courses.title: Organization and Administration of Kinesiology Programs
courses.description: A study of issues facing administrators in exercise-related professions. Special emphasis is placed on programs, policies, procedures, and problems influencing leaders in the areas of health, physical education, recreation and sports. Prerequisites: KIN 1003, 1113, and 2093 for KIN Major; Junior standing for Business Administration Major with Sport Management Emphasis. [CW3] Fall, Spring.
courses.prereq_text: KIN 1003, 1113, and 2093 for KIN Major; Junior standing for Business Administration Major with Sport Management Emphasis

courses.subject: KIN
courses.title: Field Experience in KIN-Senior BA (Non-Teaching Emphasis) Candidates Only
courses.description: This class represents the culmination experience of our undergraduate degree program. It will be used as a “steppingstone” for employment for students. It is viewed as an “apprenticeship” as students will be placed under a mentor in the field outside the university setting. Field experiences are generally 10 weeks in length. Classroom experience will be prior to and after the field experience. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: KIN
courses.title: Exercise Prescription and Testing
courses.description: A study of the guidelines for exercise prescription, programming, and testing for generally healthy persons as advised by the American College of Sports Medicine and the National Strength and Conditioning Association. Prerequisites: KIN 3023. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: KIN
courses.title: Biomechanical Analysis
courses.description: A study of body movements, of muscle and joint action in relation to physical activity. Mechanical analysis of the more commo nly used physical skills is studied. Prerequisite: KIN 1003, 1113, KIN 2093 or BIOL 2014. Fall.

courses.subject: KIN
courses.title: Health Education and Counseling
courses.description: This course introduces students to the foundations of health education and the essential counseling skills used to promote po sitive health behavior change. Students will explore major theoretical models —such as the Health Belief Model, Social Cognitive The ory, Transtheoretical Model, Ecological Models, and theories of stress and coping—and learn how these frameworks inform effective health promotion strategies. Fa…

courses.subject: KIN
courses.title: Methods and Materials in Health, PE, and Wellness Education
courses.description: The theory and methods utilized in effective health, physical education, and wellness instruction. Prerequisite: KIN 1003. Fall.

courses.subject: KIN
courses.title: Personal Trainer
courses.description: This advanced elective course is designed to prepare students to integrate strength and conditioning knowledge and skills obt ained in specific coursework and to apply this in preparation for the National Council on Strength and Fitness (NCSF) Personal Trai ning certification exam. Students completing this course will have the opportunity to sit for the NCSF exam. Prerequisites: KIN 1003, 1113, 2093, and 4043. On Dem…

courses.subject: KIN
courses.title: Senior Seminar
courses.description: This seminar encourages students to integrate knowledge and skills from their major field of study with the broader liberal arts experience provided by the Ouachita Core Curriculum. The course provides a basis for life-long learning, meaningful work, and service to humans in a diverse and interconnected world. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: KIN
courses.title: Health Promotion Seminar
courses.description: This course will focus on community health needs in specific demographic areas of need. Students will be engaged in improving health literacy for select populations. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: KIN
courses.title: Special Studies
courses.description: A course designed to provide an opportunity to do advanced research or independent work in an area of special interest. On Demand.

courses.subject: LATN
courses.title: Elementary Latin I
courses.description: An introduction to classical Latin. The course focuses on grammar, syntax, and vocabulary. On Demand.

courses.subject: LATN
courses.title: Elementary Latin II
courses.description: A continuation of LATN 2203. On Demand.

courses.subject: LATN
courses.title: Intermediate Latin I
courses.description: A course focusing on the upper reaches of classical Latin grammar and syntax. On Demand.

courses.subject: LATN
courses.title: Intermediate Latin II
courses.description: A course focusing on the translation of various classical Latin poems and prose pieces. On Demand.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: College Algebra
courses.description: A study of the properties and applications of linear, exponential, logarithmic, quadratic, and polynomial functions, as well as an introduction to absolute value, piecewise, and rational functions. Additional topics will include transformation and composit ion of functions, as well as matrices and their use in the solution of linear systems. Prerequisite: An MPI of 75 or higher. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: College Algebra with Review
courses.description: A version of MATH 1003 with additional contact hours in order to provide just-in-time review and extra support. Prerequisite: An MPI of 65 or higher, or a grade of C or better in ASKL 1023. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Mathematics for the Liberal Arts
courses.description: Students will engage in a study of mathematical ideas and thinking, learning to solve problems and make decisions using sound quantitative reasoning. All students will study techniques of problem-solving, mathematical reasoning, the set of real numbers, sizes of infinity, and the use of analogy to explore four-dimensional geometry. prereq_other: An MPI of 65 or higher, or a grade of C or better in ASKL 1023

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Precalculus
courses.description: A course designed to prepare students for Calculus. Topics include functions, polynomials, rational functions, exponential an d logarithmic functions, circular functions, systems of linear equations and coordinate geometry. Prerequisite: An MPI of 80 or higher, or a grade of C or better in MATH 1003 or MATH 1004. Fall.

courses.title: Introduction to Cryptology
courses.description: This course explores the science of communication security. courses.title: Calculus I
courses.description: Introductory study of calculus and analytic geometry, including differentiation, application of derivatives, integration, and application of integrals. Prerequisite: An MPI of 85 or higher, or a grade of C or better in MATH 1034. Spring.

courses.title: Elementary Statistics
courses.description: An introduction to the fundamental concepts and methods of modern statistics, emphasizing data analysis and statistical reaso ning. courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Discrete Mathematics
courses.description: An introduction to the techniques of mathematical proof. Additional topics in number and graph theory, equivalence relations, functions, combinatorics, and algebraic group theory. Prerequisite: MATH 1103. Fall.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Number Sense and Operations
courses.description: An introduction to the mathematical concepts underlying the traditional computational techniques for elementary school mathem atics, and to instructional methods that can be used to teach these ideas at the elementary school level. Open only to students maj oring in Elementary Education. Prerequisite: An MPI of 65 or higher, or a grade of C or better in ASKL 1023. Fall.

prereq_other: An MPI of 65 or higher, or a grade of C or better in ASKL 1023

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Number Sense and Operations for Middle School Teachers
courses.description: An introduction to the mathematical concepts underlying the traditional computational techniques for elementary and middle sc hool mathematics, and to instructional methods that can be used to teach these ideas at the middle school level. Open only to stud ents majoring in Middle School Education. Prerequisite: An MPI of 65 or higher, or a grade of C or better in ASKL 1023. Fall.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Foundations of Geometry
courses.description: A study of the axiomatic bases of geometries, their relation to “real’’ space; basic concepts of point, line, plane and space ; projective and non-Euclidean geometries. Prerequisite: MATH 2014 or 2343. Spring of even-numbered years.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Calculus III
courses.description: Continuation of MATH 2024. A study of polar coordinates, vectors, vector -valued functions, functions of multiple variables, including partial differentiation and multiple integrals. Prerequisite: MATH 2024. Spring.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Differential Equations
courses.description: Use of differential equations to model phenomena in sciences and engineering. Solution of differential equations via analytic, qualitative, and numerical techniques. Linear and nonlinear systems of differential equations. Laplace transforms. Prerequisite: MATH 2024. Fall.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Abstract Algebra I
courses.description: A study of groups: symmetric groups, groups of integers, subgroups, group homomorphisms and isomorphisms, and other group theory topics. Prerequisites: MATH 2343. Spring of odd-numbered years.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Probability and Statistics
courses.description: Counting techniques, probability, odds, mathematical expectation, distributions, moments, sampling, mathematical models and t esting hypotheses. Prerequisite: MATH 2024. Spring of even-numbered years.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Linear Algebra
courses.description: A study of vectors, matrices, and their applications. Topics include linear systems, matrix algebra, matrix factorizations, r eal vector spaces, determinants, eigenvectors and eigenvalues, orthogonality and least squares, diagonalization, and the singular v alue decomposition. Prerequisite: MATH 1103 or MATH 2014 or consent of instructor. Fall of even-numbered years.
courses.prereq_text: MATH 1103 or MATH 2014 or consent of instructor
prereq_other: MATH 1103 or MATH 2014 or consent of instructor

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Geometry and Algebra
courses.description: Basic ideas of geometry, including plane regions and space figures, measurement, relations, functions and graphs, linear equa tions, and logic. Instructional methods that can be used to teach these ideas at the elementary school level. Open only to students majoring in Elementary Education. Prerequisite: MATH 2123. Spring.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Probability, Data Analysis, and Computing
courses.description: Basic ideas of probability, data analysis, and computing, and instructional methods that can be used to teach these ideas at the elementary school level. Open only to students majoring in Elementary Education. Prerequisite: MATH 2123. Fall.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Geometry and Algebra for Middle School Teachers
courses.description: Basic ideas of geometry, including plane regions and space figures, measurement, relations, functions and graphs, linear equa tions, and logic. Instructional methods that can be used to teach these ideas at the middle school level. Open only to students maj oring in Middle School Education. Prerequisite: MATH 2223. Spring.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Probability, Data Analysis, and Computing for Middle School Teachers
courses.description: Basic ideas of probability, data analysis, and computing, and instructional methods that can be used to teach these ideas at the middle school level. Open only to students majoring in Middle School Education. Prerequisite: MATH 2223. Fall.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Advanced Chemical Calculations
courses.description: A study of calculations required to master advanced chemical topics. This course may not be counted towards a major in mathematics. Prerequisite: MATH 2014. Prerequisite or corequisite: CHEM 3104. Spring.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Methods in Secondary Mathematics
courses.description: A modular course for secondary mathematics education students including theories, purposes, activities, curricula and new developments in teaching. Prerequisite: Approval to do student teaching. Fall.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Introduction to Real Analysis
courses.description: A more theoretical treatment than is provided by the basic calculus courses. Topics include limits, continuity, derivatives a nd the Riemann integral; primarily in one dimension. Prerequisites: MATH 2024 and 2343. On Demand.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Further Studies in Real Analysis
courses.description: Continuation of MATH 4023. Topics include series, functions of several variables and integrals other than Riemann -type. Prerequisite: MATH 4023. On Demand.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Abstract Algebra II
courses.description: Continuation of MATH 3053. Study of rings, fields, polynomial rings, extension fields, Galois Theory, and other topics. Prerequisites: MATH 3053. On Demand.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Classroom Peer Instructor
courses.description: Student peer instructors will assist the instructor in the instruction of a mathematics course. Peer instructors will engage in individual and small group instruction during course review sessions, will be prepared to answer questions related to weekly cou rse exercises, and may assist in the preparation, administration, and grading of assignments. Peer instructors may be required to design a classroom activity and/o…

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Special Topics in Mathematics
courses.description: A course covering special mathematical content not normally covered in the curriculum. Course may be repeated for credit one time, provided that the repeat is a different topic. Prerequisite: Consent of instructor. Spring of even-numbered years.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Mathematical Scholarship
courses.description: Students will engage in independent learning activities, reading of technical literature, and communication of mathematical r esults in both written and oral form. Assignments will focus on the connection of mathematics to the liberal arts, on the historical development of mathematics, and on the use of mathematical models to solve applied mathematics problems. This work will lead to a senior pro ject suitable for pr…

prereq_other: Senior standing or consent of instructor

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Special Studies in Mathematics
courses.description: For students who wish to do independent work on advanced problems. On Demand.

courses.title: Mathematics for Secondary Teachers
courses.description: Further studies of the mathematical concepts underlying the traditional curriculum for secondary school mathematics. Prerequisite: Junior standing or consent of instructor. Spring of odd-numbered years.

courses.subject: MGMT
courses.title: Business Communications
courses.description: A focus on oral and written business communication with emphasis on individual and group presentations incorporating current presentation technology. Prerequisite: DLIT 1013. [CW2] Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: MGMT
courses.title: Management Information Systems
courses.description: The study of management information systems design and implementation. Includes coverage of current software packages availab le and various types of computer-based systems. Prerequisite: DLIT 1013. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: MGMT
courses.title: Organization Behavior and Management
courses.description: The study of managing individuals and small groups in the workplace. Topics include individual motivation in the work place, groups at work, power and social influence, managerial leadership, managing change and conflict, and principles of management. Prer equisite: Junior standing. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: MGMT
courses.title: Human Resources Management
courses.description: Determination of personnel requirements, recruitment of needed employees, testing and training methods, supervision, compensa tion and benefits, introduction to labor relations, and legal matters. Prerequisite: MGMT 3043. Spring.

courses.subject: MGMT
courses.title: Production and Operations Management
courses.description: The study of the concepts, principles, and techniques of production of goods and services within time and resource constraints. Topics include decision theory, forecasting, facility planning, inventory and quality control, and project management. Prerequisites: DLIT 2033 or consent of the instructor. Fall, Spring.
courses.prereq_text: DLIT 2033 or consent of the instructor
prereq_other: DLIT 2033 or consent of the instructor

courses.subject: MGMT
courses.title: Business Leadership
courses.description: The study of theories and practices used by leaders towards the achievement of their goals. Primary topics include (1) syner getic thinking and methods, (2) organizational culture, and (3) persuasion of others via both automatic and effortful cognitive pro cesses. Prerequisite: MGMT 3043. Fall.

courses.subject: MGMT
courses.title: Management Strategy and Policy
courses.description: This course is designed to integrate the knowledge which the student has acquired in all prior course work; the case method w ill be used. Open only to seniors in the School of Business. Prerequisites: MKTG 3033, MGMT 3043, FINN 3013. Spring.

courses.subject: MGMT
courses.title: Special Studies in Management
courses.description: Given on demand and varied to meet the needs of seniors. On Demand.

courses.subject: MGMT
courses.title: Management Internship
courses.description: This class is an applied integrative experience in management where students learn and work under a mentor in the field outside the university setting. These will generally be 400 hours in length. Prerequisite: Junior Standing. Summer, On Demand.

courses.subject: MKTG
courses.title: Principles of Marketing
courses.description: An introduction to the system of activities that constitute marketing: product or service planning and development, pricing, promotion and distribution, with emphasis on the principles, policies and strategies utilized to satisfy the needs and wants of the consumers and society. Prerequisites: ACCT 2013, ECON 2023, or consent of the instructor. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: MKTG
courses.title: Transportation and Channels Management
courses.description: Management of distribution functions such as purchasing, transportation, storage, packaging, and handling. Focuses on the characteristics, functions, and interrelationships of the producer, transportation, retail, and wholesale institutions in the marketing channel. Prerequisite: MKTG 3033. Spring.

courses.subject: MKTG
courses.title: Consumer Behavior
courses.description: The study of the contribution to marketing from the social sciences in the areas of individual and group behavior. Prerequisi te: MKTG 3033. Fall.

courses.description: This lab focuses on the development of students interested in developing leadership skills through concrete experiences. courses.subject: MSCI
courses.title: Foundations of Leadership
courses.description: MSCI 1021 introduces cadets to the personal challenges and competencies that are critical for effective leadership. Cadets learn the personal development of life skills such as critical thinking, time management, goal setting, and communication. Cadets learn the basics of the communications process and the importance for leaders to develop the essential skills to effectively communicate in the Army. Cadets will begin…

courses.title: Military Leadership and Ethics
courses.description: focuses on leadership and ethics. The course adds depth to the cadet's knowledge of the different leadership styles. courses.description: MSCI 2042 focuses on Army doctrine and decision making. courses.description: MSCI 3053 focuses on training management and the warfighting functions. courses.description: MSCI 3063 focuses on applied leadership in small unit operations. courses.title: U.S. Military History
courses.description: In this course, students will study the history of the U.S. military. This course builds an understanding of and integrates the principles and practices of changing economic, society and world events. Students will gain knowledge about the history of major American military operations, wars, and conflicts from past to current era.

courses.subject: MSCI
courses.title: The Army Officer
courses.description: MSCI 4073 focuses on development of the Army Officer. It is an academically challenging course where you will develop knowledge, skills, and abilities to plan, resource, and assess training at the small unit level. You will also learn about Army programs that support counseling subordinates and evaluating performance, values and ethics, career planning, and legal responsibilities. courses.subject: MSCI
courses.title: Company Grade Leadership
courses.description: MSCI 4083 is an academically challenging course where you will develop knowledge, skills, and abilities required of junior officers focused on Company Grade Officer roles and responsibilities. This course includes reading assignments, homework assignments, small group assignments, briefings, case studies, practical exercises, a midterm exam, and an Oral Practicum as the final exam. The Oral Practicum explores your kn…

courses.subject: MSCI
courses.title: Independent Study in Leadership
courses.description: The ROTC program APMS will conduct leadership classes with students and assign additional coursework as needed to develop the student into a successful Army officer. This is only for MS5 status students. Corequisite: MSCI 1000. Fall, Spring.
prereq_other: This is only for MS5 status students.

courses.subject: MSED
courses.title: Reading: Children’s Literature
courses.description: A survey of sources and types of reading materials available for children with an emphasis on reading comprehension and an introduction to the science of reading. Spring.

courses.subject: MSED
courses.title: Teaching of Social Studies
courses.description: Methods and materials for teaching social studies with an emphasis on economics and the integration of multicultural education and inclusion into the social studies curriculum. Pre-requisite: Admission to Teacher Education. Fall.

courses.subject: MSED
courses.title: Middle School Methods and Classroom Management
courses.description: An examination of the philosophy and organizational patterns of the middle school, the unique learning characteristics of middle school students and the appropriate methods for teaching them. Pre-requisite: EDFN 2003. Spring.

courses.subject: MSED
courses.title: Reading: Foundations
courses.description: A study of the science or reading including foundational skills, models and theories of reading, and instructional strategies utilized in a systematic and explicit manner for teaching reading. All elements of the science of teaching reading including phonics, phonemic awareness, fluency, vocabulary, and comprehension will be addressed. The field component of this class will provide the opportunity to apply the concep…

courses.subject: MSED
courses.title: Reading and Writing
courses.description: A study of the integration of reading and writing, with emphasis on vocabulary strategies, process writing, and awareness of the science of reading. The field component of this class will provide the opportunity for students to apply a variety of reading and writing strategies. Prerequisite: Admission to Teacher Education. Spring.

courses.subject: MSED
courses.title: Reading: Diagnostic
courses.description: A study of diagnosing reading readiness and implementing strategies for improving reading instruction based on individual student needs. Use of informal reading inventories, standardized testing, various screenings, and other sources will be presented and implemented to assist with diagnosing reading needs. Prerequisite: Admission to Teacher Education. Fall.

courses.subject: MSED
courses.title: Special Studies in Education
courses.description: Provides advanced students with an opportunity to pursue independent study on significant education problems. On Demand.

courses.subject: MUAP
courses.title: Performing Arts Class
courses.description: Performing Arts Class is required of all students who are studying toward a degree in music. A grade is given based on the student's attendance at Performing Arts Class and at recitals and concerts at Ouachita and off campus. A statement of attendance requirements is available in the Division of Music office. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: MUAP
courses.title: Piano Seminar
courses.description: A course that surveys the professional world of the pianist, including topics such as piano literature, performance practices, careers for pianists, and performance skills. Required of piano majors and minors each semester when enrolled for applied music credit. A grade is assigned based on the student's attendance at a weekly class meeting. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: MUAP
courses.title: Class Piano I
courses.description: This course is designed for non-keyboard majors who have a minimum or no experience at the piano. The course will introduce basic musicianship elements applying concepts and terminology from music theory, aural skills, and keyboard skills. The material covered will include scales, chord progressions, harmonization, transposition, sight-reading, ensemble playing, and performance of elementary level piano literature. S…
courses.prereq_text: A placement audition with the piano faculty.
prereq_other: A placement audition with the piano faculty.

courses.subject: MUAP
courses.title: Class Piano II
courses.description: Continuation of Class Piano I. Material covered during this level will be based on and expand the rudimentary skills acquired in Piano Class I. Students must earn a C or better to pass and advance to Piano Class II. Pre-requisite: Class Piano I. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: MUAP
courses.title: Vocal Diction 1
courses.description: A study of the International Phonetic Alphabet and English, Italian, and Latin diction. Fall.

courses.subject: MUAP
courses.title: Vocal Diction 2
courses.description: A study of German and French diction. Prerequisite: MUAP 1272. Spring of Odd-numbered Years.

courses.subject: MUAP
courses.title: Piano Accompanying
courses.description: A half-hour course that meets once a week for one hour to provide sophomore, junior, and senior pianists basic skills and practical experience for vocal and instrumental accompanying. Skills covered include sight-reading; score-reading/rearranging; figured bass (continuo); learning music quickly; listening and reacting to diverse musical intentions; and contributing to ensemble accuracy. Piano principals in the Bache…
prereq_other: Consent of instructor is required for registration.

courses.subject: MUAP
courses.title: Guitar Class I
courses.description: This course is designed for non-guitar majors who have minimum or no experience at the guitar. The course will introduce basic musicianship elements applying concepts and terminology from music theory specifically related to the guitar fretboard and songwriting. The material covered will include open scales, chord progressions in the first position, transposition using a capo, sight-reading tablature, group playing,…
courses.prereq_text: A placement audition with the guitar instructor.
prereq_other: A placement audition with the guitar instructor.

courses.subject: MUAP
courses.title: Guitar Class II
courses.description: This course is a continuation of MUAP 1471 Guitar Class I. The course will expand the students' knowledge of the guitar fretboard beyond first position. The material will advance to include closed position scales, improvisation, and chord progressions using CAGED barre chords. Pre-requisite: A placement audition with the guitar instructor or a grade of C or higher in MUAP 1471 Guitar Class I. Spring.
courses.prereq_text: A placement audition with the guitar instructor or a grade of C or higher in MUAP 1471 Guitar Class I.
prereq_other: A placement audition with the guitar instructor.

courses.subject: MUAP
courses.title: Class Piano III
courses.description: This class is designed for BME, BA Worship Studies, and BM Performance students who have completed Class Piano I and II. The course is a continuation of Class Piano II. The curriculum consists of more advanced piano skills including but not limited to open score reading, transposing instruments, four-part Hymn playing, and accompanying skills. Students must earn a C or better to pass this class. Prerequisite: Class P…

courses.subject: MUAP
courses.title: Class Piano IV
courses.description: This class is designed for BME, BM Worship Studies, and BM performance majors who are planning to take the Piano Proficiency Examination. Advanced students who have prior keyboard training may enroll in this course for assistance in preparing for the Piano Proficiency Examination. Students must earn a C or better to pass this class. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: MUED
courses.title: Introduction to Music Education
courses.description: A course designed to introduce the undergraduate student to the foundations and principles of music education in schools. Students will be introduced to topics including history and philosophy of music education, learning theories as they apply to music education, institutional requirements, sequence of courses, and deadlines for the degree. Spring.

courses.subject: MUED
courses.title: Brass Methods
courses.description: Teaching techniques for brass instruments with elementary playing facility on each. Music majors only. Fall.

courses.subject: MUED
courses.title: Woodwind Methods
courses.description: A survey of teaching techniques and elementary performance practices on woodwind instruments. For music majors and minors only. Spring.
prereq_other: For music majors and minors only.

courses.subject: MUED
courses.title: Elementary Music Methods and Materials
courses.description: A course designed to educate the music specialist in the teaching of elementary music in public schools (Grades P-6). Song singing, dramatization, listening, rhythmic responses, rhythmic instruments, keyboard experience and creative expression are included. The student will also obtain knowledge, understanding and method of use of music technology for the elementary classroom and ePortfolios. Music Majors only. Prere…
courses.prereq_text: MUED 1021 Introduction to Music Education & EDFN 2003 Foundations for Education or consent of the instructor.

courses.subject: MUED
courses.title: Principles of Conducting
courses.description: An introduction to the fundamentals of conducting. Fall.

courses.subject: MUED
courses.title: Secondary Choral Methods and Materials
courses.description: A study of the musical needs of the junior high and senior high schools (grades 7-12). The course examines programs, procedures, and materials. The student will also obtain knowledge, understanding and methods of use of music technology for the secondary classroom. Music Majors only. Spring.

courses.subject: MUED
courses.title: Percussion Methods
courses.description: A survey of methods and materials for percussion instruments. Students will gain a playing facility in one instrument plus a working knowledge of the remaining instruments in the group. For music majors only. Spring.

courses.subject: MUED
courses.title: Choral Conducting
courses.description: Advanced study of the theory and practice of conducting choral ensembles. Spring.

courses.subject: MUED
courses.title: Instrumental Conducting
courses.description: Advanced study of the theory and practice of conducting instrumental ensembles. Spring.

courses.subject: MUED
courses.title: Vocal Pedagogy
courses.description: This course will review the anatomy and physiology of the singing mechanism, focusing on respiration, phonation, resonance, and articulation in different styles of singing, including classical and contemporary commercial music genres. Students will explore basic, practical, and detailed approaches in voice production based on diverse traditional and modern vocal pedagogy literature. Emphasis is on the familiarity and…

courses.subject: MUED
courses.title: Piano Pedagogy
courses.description: A study of drill methods, fundamentals, teaching materials, and principal problems of piano teaching. Open to all students with freshman piano major facility. On Demand.
prereq_other: Open to all students with freshman piano major facility.

courses.subject: MUED
courses.title: Organ Pedagogy
courses.description: A study of the methods and materials for teaching organ. Preparation of lesson plans for one semester of organ lessons and the teaching of students as a laboratory experience is included. Prerequisites: Organ principal and consent of instructor. On Demand.
courses.prereq_text: Organ principal and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUED
courses.title: Secondary Instrumental Methods and Materials
courses.description: A course designed to expose students to the functions of a band director in relation to the organization of a total band program (Grades 7-12). Emphasis on public relations, budgeting, marching techniques, concert and contest preparation. The student will also obtain knowledge, understanding and method of use of music technology for the secondary classroom and e-Portfolios. Music majors only. Spring.

courses.subject: MUED
courses.title: Practicum in Music Education K-12
courses.description: Designed to enable candidates to understand the principles of student development and to better inform teacher decision making for All-level music students. Candidates will be provided an intense field experience component. The course will also provide an overview of the basis for music organization and appropriate teaching strategies characteristic of the music program, including scheduling, curriculum design, and s…

courses.subject: MUED
courses.title: Music Student Teaching I
courses.description: Provides for observation, participation, and responsible music teaching experience in a public school system. Concurrent enrollment required in EDFN 4403 and MUED 4414. Prerequisites: Approval to do student teaching. Fall, Spring.
courses.coreq_text: Concurrent enrollment required in EDFN 4403 and MUED 4414.

courses.subject: MUED
courses.title: Music Student Teaching II
courses.description: Provides for observation, participation, and responsible music teaching experience in a public school system. Concurrent enrollment required in EDFN 4403 and MUED 4405. Prerequisites: Approval to do student teaching. Fall, Spring.
courses.coreq_text: Concurrent enrollment required in EDFN 4403 and MUED 4405.

courses.subject: MUED
courses.title: Music Student Teaching III
courses.description: Provides for observation, participation, and responsible music teaching experience in a public school system. Concurrent enrollment required in EDFN 4403, MUED 4414 and MUED 4405. Prerequisites: Approval to do student teaching. Fall, Spring.
courses.coreq_text: Concurrent enrollment required in EDFN 4403, MUED 4414 and MUED 4405.

courses.subject: MUEN
courses.title: Concert Choir
courses.description: Membership in this organization is open to any student desiring choral experience at the university level. Its repertoire includes a wide range of literature from simple folk songs to extended compositions. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: MUEN
courses.title: Ouachita Worship
courses.description: The purpose of Ouachita Worship is to study, prepare and lead worship for weekly chapel. Membership is based on audition. May be repeated for elective credit after the requirements for the major have been met. Prerequisite: Sophomore standing. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: MUEN
courses.title: Piano Ensemble
courses.description: Study and performance of literature for two or more pianists. Prerequisite: Consent of the instructor.

courses.subject: MUEN
courses.title: Gospel Choir
courses.description: The MORE Gospel Choir performs Gospel Music from traditional Spiritual arrangements to Modern and Contemporary Gospel. Membership is open to all interested students. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: MUEN
courses.title: Opera Theatre Production
courses.description: By participating in the production of an operatic work or opera scenes, students will gain experience performing in and creating all aspects of an operatic production. In addition to learning operatic repertoire, students will be trained in vocal development, stage deportment, theatrical terminology, and acting technique. Admittance by audition or personal interview with the director. Required of all voice performanc…
prereq_other: Admittance by audition or personal interview with the director.

courses.subject: MUEN
courses.title: Ouachita Singers
courses.description: Membership in this organization will be achieved through audition or a personal interview with the director. Public performances and annual tour are required. Fall, Spring.
prereq_other: Membership by audition or a personal interview with the director.

courses.subject: MUEN
courses.title: Jazz Band
courses.description: Study and performance in the field of jazz and other forms of popular music. Membership by audition or consent of director. Fall, Spring.
prereq_other: Membership by audition or consent of director.

courses.subject: MUEN
courses.title: Musical Theatre Workshop
courses.description: A practical application in the basic skills of acting, movement, singing, stagecraft, makeup, musical theatre directing and production. Membership by audition or invitation. Double-listed as THEA 1151.* Spring.

courses.subject: MUEN
courses.title: Marching Band
courses.description: Membership is open to all qualified students. Fall.

courses.subject: MUEN
courses.title: Symphonic Band
courses.description: Membership open to all students enrolled in 1021 during the Fall semester and/or by audition and consent of director. Spring.

courses.subject: MUEN
courses.title: Steel Drum Ensemble
courses.description: Tiger Steel is a world music ensemble dedicated to the study and performance of Caribbean music, primarily calypso and soca from Trinidad and Tobago, and secondarily Latin, Brazilian, reggae, funk, rock, jazz, classical, and popular music styles. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: MUEN
courses.title: Flute Ensemble
courses.description: Survey of chamber flute literature, pedagogy, performance practices, and performance skills. Required of all flute majors and minors each semester when enrolled for applied music credit. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: MUEN
courses.title: Double Reed Ensemble
courses.description: Survey of chamber double reed literature, pedagogy, performance practices, and performance skills. Required of all double reed majors and minors each semester when enrolled for applied music credit. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: MUEN
courses.title: Clarinet Ensemble
courses.description: Survey of chamber clarinet literature, pedagogy, performance practices, and performance skills. Required of all clarinet majors and minors each semester when enrolled for applied music credit. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: MUEN
courses.title: Saxophone Ensemble
courses.description: Survey of chamber saxophone literature, pedagogy, performance practices, and performance skills. Required of all saxophone majors and minors each semester when enrolled for applied music credit. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: MUEN
courses.title: Trumpet Ensemble
courses.description: Survey of chamber trumpet literature, pedagogy, performance practices, and performance skills. Required of all trumpet majors and minors each semester when enrolled for applied music credit. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: MUEN
courses.title: Horn Ensemble
courses.description: Survey of chamber horn literature, pedagogy, performance practices, and performance skills. Required of all horn majors and minors each semester when enrolled for applied music credit. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: MUEN
courses.title: Trombone Ensemble
courses.description: Survey of chamber trombone literature, pedagogy, performance practices, and performance skills. Required of all trombone majors and minors each semester when enrolled for applied music credit. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: MUEN
courses.title: Euphonium/Tuba Ensemble
courses.description: Survey of chamber euphonium/tuba literature, pedagogy, performance practices, and performance skills. Required of all euphonium/tuba majors and minors each semester when enrolled for applied music credit. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: MUEN
courses.title: String Ensemble
courses.description: Study and performance of chamber music literature for string ensembles. Membership by audition or invitation. On Demand.

courses.subject: MUEN
courses.title: Ouachita Handbell Ringers
courses.description: An ensemble designed to teach the art of handbell ringing with emphasis on techniques, care of the bells, literature and uses of handbells in church and school. Membership by audition or invitation. Prerequisite: Proficiency in reading music. On Demand.

courses.subject: MUEN
courses.title: Percussion Ensemble
courses.description: Survey of percussion literature, pedagogy, performance practices, and performance skills. Required of all percussion majors and minors each semester when enrolled for applied music credit. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: MUEN
courses.title: Guitar Ensemble
courses.description: This course is designed to prepare guitarist for varying roles in practical, traditional and creative aspects of performing a variety of technical styles conducive to specific musical genres, with a special focus on improvisation. Required of all guitar majors and minors each semester when enrolled for applied music credit. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: MUEN
courses.title: Wind Ensemble
courses.description: The purpose of the wind ensemble is to study and perform quality sacred and secular wind and percussion literature. Membership is based on an audition. Fall, Spring.
prereq_other: Membership is based on an audition.

courses.subject: MUEN
courses.title: Concert Choir
courses.description: Membership in this organization is open to any student desiring choral experience at the university level. Its repertoire includes a wide range of literature from simple folk songs to extended compositions. Prerequisite: Junior standing. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: MUEN
courses.title: Ouachita Singers
courses.description: Membership in this organization will be achieved through audition or a personal interview with the director. Public performances and annual tour are required. Prerequisite: Junior standing. Fall, Spring.
prereq_other: Membership by audition or a personal interview with the director.

courses.subject: MUEN
courses.title: Marching Band
courses.description: Membership is open to all qualified students. Prerequisite: Junior standing. Fall.

courses.subject: MUEN
courses.title: Symphonic Band
courses.description: Membership open to all students enrolled in 1021 during the Fall semester and/or by audition and consent of director. Prerequisite: Junior standing. Spring.

courses.subject: MUEN
courses.title: Wind Ensemble
courses.description: The purpose of the wind ensemble is to study and perform quality sacred and secular wind and percussion literature. Membership is based on an audition. Prerequisite: Junior standing. Fall, Spring.
prereq_other: Membership is based on an audition.

courses.subject: MUIN
courses.title: Introduction to the Music Industry
courses.description: An introduction to the history of the music industry with a survey of business practices and career opportunities. Fall.

courses.subject: MUIN
courses.title: Introduction to the Recording Studio
courses.description: An overview of the theory and practice of music recording, with emphasis on modern recording studio practices, including microphone placement, console and signal flow, editing, signal processing and live recording. Fall of odd-numbered years.

courses.subject: MUIN
courses.title: Copyright and Intellectual Property Law
courses.description: An introduction to copyright law and its application to creative works. Music Industry, Audio & Technical Production majors only, or permission of instructor. Spring of even-numbered years.
prereq_other: Music Industry, Audio & Technical Production majors only, or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: MUIN
courses.title: Music Publishing
courses.description: An introduction to music publishing, including composer/arranger contracts, licensing, print publishing, and copyright acquisition. Prerequisite: MUIN 1003 Intro to the Music Industry. Spring of odd-numbered years.
courses.prereq_text: MUIN 1003 Intro to the Music Industry.

courses.subject: MUIN
courses.title: History of Commercial Music
courses.description: Commercial music from the late nineteenth century to today, with emphasis on commercial music in the United States since 1950. Spring of even-numbered years.

courses.subject: MUIN
courses.title: Advanced Recording Techniques
courses.description: Further development of microphone techniques, use of processing equipment and multi-track digital recording, effects, MIDI and video/audio interlock. Prerequisite: MUIN 2003 Introduction to the Recording Studio. Spring of even-numbered years.
courses.prereq_text: MUIN 2003 Introduction to the Recording Studio.

courses.subject: MUIN
courses.title: Special Projects in Music Industry
courses.description: Students will select from various team-based project options related to the music industry. Spring of odd-numbered years.

courses.subject: MUIN
courses.title: Commercial Songwriting
courses.description: Explores lyric writing, chord progressions, melodic creation, emotional expression, song structure, and the use of a digital audio workstation as part of the creative process. May be repeated for credit without restriction. Prerequisite: MUTH 1032, MUTH 1132, or consent of the instructor. On Demand.
courses.prereq_text: MUTH 1032, MUTH 1132, or consent of the instructor.

courses.subject: MUIN
courses.title: The Musician as Entrepreneur
courses.description: The development of a successful freelance career in the music industry, including the basics of running a one-person business, lifestyle considerations, personal and professional financial management, and the exploitation of potential income streams. Prerequisite: MUIN 1003 Intro to the Music Industry. Fall of even-numbered years.
courses.prereq_text: MUIN 1003 Intro to the Music Industry.

courses.subject: MUIN
courses.title: Internship in the Music Industry
courses.description: Participation as an intern producing work for a business, civic, or educational organization. Placement and proposed work plan must be approved by the Music Industry faculty. Prerequisites: Music Industry major with senior standing. Fall, Spring, Summer.
courses.prereq_text: Music Industry major with senior standing.
prereq_other: Music Industry major with senior standing.
Placement and proposed work plan must be approved by the Music Industry faculty.

courses.subject: MUIN
courses.title: Music Production Practicum
courses.description: In-depth experience in the music production process, with emphasis on pre-production, programming, loop-based production techniques, instrumental and vocal tracking, editing, pitch correction, mixing, and mastering. Prerequisite: MUIN 3033 Advanced Recording Techniques. Fall of even-numbered years.

courses.subject: MUSC
courses.title: Survey of Music History
courses.description: Introductory examination of the periods, genres, and terminology pertinent to the basic elements of music, world music cultures, Western art music, and American music. Examination of the various styles, genres, composers, and terminology pertinent to world music cultures from Africa, Latin America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia; Western art music from antiquity to present; and American music traditions. Emphasis…

courses.subject: MUSC
courses.title: History and Literature of Musical Theatre
courses.description: A history of musical theatre with an emphasis on style and performance of representative literature. Required for all Musical Theatre degree candidates. Fall of even-numbered years.

courses.subject: MUSC
courses.title: Jazz History
courses.description: A survey of jazz music from its beginning to the present. On Demand.

courses.subject: MUSC
courses.title: World Music Cultures
courses.description: Introduction to music from a variety of world cultures and the study of world music and the ethnomusicological approach. Examination of the music from world cultures such as Indonesia, India, Ireland, West Africa, Latin America, Egypt, and China. Prerequisites: FINA 3123, MUSC 3313, or permission of instructor. Spring of odd-numbered years.
courses.prereq_text: FINA 3123, MUSC 3313, or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: MUSC
courses.title: Western Art Music
courses.description: Examination of the various styles, genres, composers, and terminology pertinent to Western music from antiquity to the present. Emphasis placed on the historical and cultural foundations of music through extensive reading, listening, research, and writing. Prerequisites: MUSC 1223 Survey of Music or permission of instructor. Spring of Even-numbered Years.
courses.prereq_text: MUSC 1223 Survey of Music or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: MUSC
courses.title: History of Modern Art Music
courses.description: Examination of the various genres of Western art music during the 20th- and 21st centuries. Extensive reading, listening, research, and writing about music of the era. Prerequisites: MUSC 3313 or permission of instructor. On Demand.

courses.subject: MUSC
courses.title: Instrumental Literature
courses.description: A survey of solo literature for wind instruments. Required of instrumental majors enrolled for the Bachelor of Music degree in Performance. Music majors only. On Demand.

courses.subject: MUSC
courses.title: History of American Music
courses.description: Examination of American music from pre-Jamestown to the present. Emphasis placed on the historical and cultural foundations of American music through extensive readings, listening, research, and writing. Prerequisites: MUSC 3313 or permission of instructor. On demand.

courses.subject: MUSC
courses.title: Organ Literature
courses.description: A survey of organ literature from the Renaissance to the present. Emphasis is given to the development and styles of the various national schools. Prerequisite: MUSC 1223. Ability to play the organ is not a prerequisite. On Demand.

courses.subject: MUSC
courses.title: Choral Literature and Arranging
courses.description: A survey of choral literature for the public schools with emphasis on analysis and arranging. Fall of even-numbered years.

courses.subject: MUSC
courses.title: Piano Literature
courses.description: A survey of piano solo literature from 1700 to 1900 with emphasis on style and performance practices. Required of piano majors enrolled for the Bachelor of Music in Piano Performance degree. Music majors only. On Demand.

courses.subject: MUSC
courses.title: Vocal Literature
courses.description: A study of solo literature from the Renaissance to the present. Emphasis upon the style, interpretation, and performance of solo materials for all voice classifications. Required of voice majors enrolled for the Bachelor of Music in Vocal Performance degree. Music majors only. Spring of odd-numbered years.

courses.subject: MUSC
courses.title: Band History and Literature
courses.description: A survey of band and wind ensemble literature beginning with the 16th century through the present. On Demand.

courses.subject: MUSC
courses.title: Studies in Musicology (Variable Topics)
courses.description: A variable topic course examining the history of specific genres throughout music history. Topic to be chosen by instructor prior to semester offered. Emphasis placed on the historical and cultural foundations of the chosen topic through extensive reading, listening, research, and writing. Prerequisites: MUSC 3313 or permission of instructor. May be repeated once for credit with different topic. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: MUTH
courses.title: Aural Skills 1
courses.description: A course designed to develop the sight-reading and aural abilities of the student. Exercises in syllable singing, melodic and rhythmic dictation, and aural recognition of intervals and chords are included. Spring.

courses.subject: MUTH
courses.title: Aural Skills 2
courses.description: A course designed to develop the sight-reading and aural abilities of the student. Exercises in syllable singing, melodic and rhythmic dictation, and aural recognition of intervals and chords are included. Prerequisite: MUTH 1002 Aural Skills 1 or MUTH 1102 Aural Skills for Musical Theatre & Music Industry 1. Fall.
courses.prereq_text: MUTH 1002 Aural Skills 1 or MUTH 1102 Aural Skills for Musical Theatre & Music Industry 1.

courses.subject: MUTH
courses.title: Theory 1
courses.description: A study of diatonic harmony, rhythm, meter, and basic counterpoint; an introduction to embellishing tones; and an introduction to the use of technology with practical applications in digital music notation. Spring.

courses.subject: MUTH
courses.title: Theory 2
courses.description: A continuation of MUTH 1022 with the inclusion of a study of phrase structure and tonicization. Prerequisite: A grade of C or higher in MUTH 1022 Theory 1 or MUTH 1122 Theory 1 for Musical Theater & Music Industry. Fall.
courses.prereq_text: A grade of C or higher in MUTH 1022 Theory 1 or MUTH 1122 Theory 1 for Musical Theater & Music Industry.

courses.subject: MUTH
courses.title: Aural Skills for Musical Theatre & Music Industry 1
courses.description: A course for students in the BFA Musical Theatre and BA Music Industry programs that is designed to develop the sight reading and aural abilities of the student. Exercises in syllable singing, melodic and rhythmic dictation, and aural recognition of intervals and chords are included. There will be an emphasis on musical theatre and popular music examples. Spring, Fall.

courses.subject: MUTH
courses.title: Aural Skills for Musical Theatre & Music Industry 2
courses.description: A course for students in the BFA Musical Theatre and BA Music Industry programs that is designed to develop the sight reading and aural abilities of the student. Exercises in syllable singing, melodic and rhythmic dictation, and aural recognition of intervals and chords are included. There will be an emphasis on musical theatre and popular music examples. Spring, Fall.

courses.subject: MUTH
courses.title: Theory 1 for Musical Theatre & Music Industry
courses.description: A course for students in the BFA Musical Theatre and BA Music Industry programs that includes a study of diatonic harmony, embellishing tones, and phrase structure through classical, musical theatre, and popular music. Spring.

courses.subject: MUTH
courses.title: Theory 2 for Musical Theatre & Music Industry
courses.description: A continuation of MUTH 1122 with the inclusion of a study of tonicization, form, and modulation through classical, musical theatre, and popular music. This course is intended for students in the BFA Musical Theatre and BA Music Industry programs. Prerequisite: A grade of C or higher in MUTH 1122 Theory 1 for Musical Theatre & Music Industry or MUTH 1022 Theory 1. Fall.
courses.prereq_text: A grade of C or higher in MUTH 1122 Theory 1 for Musical Theatre & Music Industry or MUTH 1022 Theory 1.

courses.subject: MUTH
courses.title: Fundamentals of Music Theory
courses.description: A course designed to prepare students for MUTH 1002 and 1022 through the study of notation, intervals, key signatures, scales, triads, seventh chords, diatonic Roman numeral analysis, meter, rhythm, and aural skills. This course does not count toward hours required for graduation. Fall.

courses.subject: MUTH
courses.title: Songwriting Practicum
courses.description: A weekly seminar dedicated to student and faculty performances, various discussion topics, master classes, guest artists, and workshops. Prerequisite: MUTH 1032 Music Theory 2 or consent of the instructor. On Demand.
courses.prereq_text: MUTH 1032 Music Theory 2 or consent of the instructor.

courses.subject: MUTH
courses.title: Aural Skills 3
courses.description: An advanced continuation of 1002, 1012. Prerequisites: MUTH 1012 Aural Skills 2 or MUTH 1112 Aural Skills for Musical Theatre & Music Industry 2. Spring, Fall.
courses.prereq_text: MUTH 1012 Aural Skills 2 or MUTH 1112 Aural Skills for Musical Theatre & Music Industry 2.

courses.subject: MUTH
courses.title: Aural Skills 4
courses.description: An advanced continuation of 1002, 1012. Prerequisites: MUTH 1012 Aural Skills 2 or MUTH 1112 Aural Skills for Musical Theatre & Music Industry 2. Spring, Fall.
courses.prereq_text: MUTH 1012 Aural Skills 2 or MUTH 1112 Aural Skills for Musical Theatre & Music Industry 2.

courses.subject: MUTH
courses.title: Theory 3
courses.description: A continuation of MUTH 1032 with a study of chromatic harmony and form. Prerequisite: A grade of C or higher in MUTH 1032 Theory 2 or MUTH 1132 Theory 2 for Musical Theater & Music Industry. Spring.
courses.prereq_text: A grade of C or higher in MUTH 1032 Theory 2 or MUTH 1132 Theory 2 for Musical Theater & Music Industry.

courses.subject: MUTH
courses.title: Theory 4
courses.description: A continuation of MUTH 2062 with the addition of studies in twentieth- and twenty-first century practices. Prerequisite: A grade of C or higher in MUTH 2062 Theory 3. Fall.
courses.prereq_text: A grade of C or higher in MUTH 2062 Theory 3.

courses.subject: MUTH
courses.title: Jazz Improvisation
courses.description: A study of the principles and techniques of jazz improvisation. The course includes analysis, keyboard and aural skills components as well as performance on a melodic instrument. Prerequisites: MUTH 1022 and 1032 and consent of the instructor. On Demand.
courses.prereq_text: MUTH 1022 and 1032 and consent of the instructor.

courses.subject: MUTH
courses.title: Film Scoring
courses.description: A presentation of the aesthetic, technical, and psychological issues of film music, including an historical, genre-based overview of the diverse aesthetics that shape film music, as well as scoring for short video/film cues. On Demand.

courses.subject: MUTH
courses.title: Music Composition
courses.description: Instruction in contemporary compositional practice. May be repeated for credit without restriction. Prerequisite: MUTH 1032, MUTH 1132, or consent of the instructor. Fall, Spring.
courses.prereq_text: MUTH 1032, MUTH 1132, or consent of the instructor.

courses.subject: MUTH
courses.title: Topics in Music Theory
courses.description: A variable topic course devoted to a music theory subject chosen by the instructor prior to the semester offered. May be repeated for credit with different topic. Prerequisite: MUTH 1032, MUTH 1132, or consent of the instructor. On demand.
courses.prereq_text: MUTH 1032, MUTH 1132, or consent of the instructor.

courses.subject: MUWS
courses.title: Worship Practicum
courses.description: A collective experience of all Worship Studies majors to give practical hands-on lab experience to gain proficiency in worship rehearsing and leading techniques for bands/praise teams and for worship choirs, and the sharing of training expertise provided by gifted professional guest speakers investing in our students. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: MUWS
courses.title: Foundations of Worship Ministry
courses.description: Biblical and philosophical fundamentals for ministry through music; various practical, administrative, and leadership dimensions, as well as clarification of role, self-identity, and call in the life of the minister-musician. Music majors, or with permission of instructor. Fall.
prereq_other: Music majors, or with permission of instructor.

courses.subject: MUWS
courses.title: Survey of Worship Music
courses.description: Designed to give the students an informed perspective on the evolution of worship music from the Reformation to the present. Spring.

courses.subject: MUWS
courses.title: Foundation for NexGen Worshipers
courses.description: A course dealing with the methods and techniques for junior high, senior high and adult choirs/worship teams in the local church. Emphasis is given to rehearsal procedures, repertoire, enlistment, and the changing voice. Spring.

courses.subject: MUWS
courses.title: Worship Administration and Leadership
courses.description: A practical and skill-focused overview of various dimensions of leading a worship ministry including organization, communication, team building, scheduling, staff relationships, financial accountability, professional development, etc., applicable in local church and other worship-focused ministry settings. Open to upper-level students without pre-requisites. Fall.

courses.subject: MUWS
courses.title: Technology and Media for Worship
courses.description: A practical study focusing on the application of technology (music, audio, and visual) and media design in worship settings. Prerequisites: permission of the Department Chair. Spring.

courses.subject: MUWS
courses.title: Studies in Worship Studies
courses.description: Courses offered upon demand or as announced; open to all students unless specified otherwise. Topics will vary, as may possible prerequisites; students may take more than one special study course provided the topics are different. As announced.

courses.subject: MUWS
courses.title: Song Writing and Arranging for Worship
courses.description: Students will gain knowledge and experience in writing and arranging for voices, instruments, and keyboards for congregational worship and other ministry settings. An additional focus will engage students in the discipline of song writing for ministry and worship. Prerequisite: MUTH 1032. Fall.

courses.subject: MUWS
courses.title: Directing the Rhythm Section
courses.description: Designed to prepare music ministry leaders in the practical and musical aspects of working with rhythm section instrumentalists in a variety of musical styles and genres, with a special focus on music for worship and ministry. Prerequisite: MUTH 1032. Spring.

courses.subject: MUWS
courses.title: Congregational Worship
courses.description: A study of the practices and elements of Christian worship with attention to congregational song, historical and cultural influences, and an emphasis on planning, leading, and evaluating corporate worship. Open to upper-level students without pre-requisites. Fall.

courses.subject: MUWS
courses.title: Internship
courses.description: The internship consists of a supervised worship ministry experience and must be approved in advanced by the Chair of the Department of Worship Studies and the Dean of the School of Performing Arts. Graded on a Satisfactory-Unsatisfactory basis where Satisfactory is defined as a grade of C or higher. Limited to Worship Studies majors. Fall, Spring, Summer.
prereq_other: Approval in advance by the Chair of the Department of Worship Studies and the Dean of the School of Performing Arts.

courses.subject: MUWS
courses.title: Senior Worship Project
courses.description: The student will plan, organize, and lead a worship service appropriate to an evangelical congregation, and prepare a document containing descriptions of all resources and materials as well as evaluating the theological, artistic, and practical merits. Limited to Worship Studies majors. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: NSCI
courses.title: Health Professions Seminar
courses.description: A seminar course for those students interested in pursuing a health profession career. Periodic presentations will be offered by visiting health professional representatives and students will be required to complete written assignments. A health fair may a lso be offered. This course is an expected prerequisite for all students who wish to conduct a mock interview with the Health Professions Com mittee prior to apply…

courses.subject: NSCI
courses.title: Special Topics in Natural Science
courses.description: A variable topics seminar course at the sophomore level in the environmental and natural sciences. On Demand.

courses.subject: NSCI
courses.title: Readings in Natural Science
courses.description: A self-paced reading course for Natural Science students to acquaint them with general readings in the natural sciences. Prerequisit e: Sophomore standing. Course is offered on a Satisfactory-Unsatisfactory basis. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: NSCI
courses.title: Methods of Teaching Elementary/Middle School Science
courses.description: A course for early childhood teachers and middle school teachers with an emphasis in English/History. This course includes me thods, materials, and teaching units in natural science. Prerequisites: CORE 2334, 3023. Spring.

courses.subject: NSCI
courses.title: Methods in Natural Science for Middle and Secondary Schools
courses.description: A methods course adapted to the teaching of science at the middle and secondary school level. It will involve practices, problems and trends in the sciences at this level. Emphasis will be placed upon correlating the lecture topics with computer applications and laboratory techniques. On Demand.

courses.subject: NSCI
courses.title: Health Care Pathophysiology
courses.description: This course builds on previous knowledge gained from Anatomy and Physiology I (structure), chemistry, microbiology and accompanies the concurrent course of Anatomy and Physiology II (function). It will provide an opportunity to examine health deviations an d their impact on human functioning across the lifespan. It is designed to enable the student to manage the health deviations of the individual therapeutically. Th…
courses.coreq_text: BIOL 2024, or consent of Director of Nursing

courses.subject: NSCI
courses.title: Issues in Science and Religion
courses.description: A study of the processes and products of theological reflection and scientific inquiry and the issues that arise in the inter action of the two enterprises. Also listed as PHIL 3183. Fall of even-numbered years. 3951-6. Workshop. Provides upper division students an opportunity to approach current topics and problems in a cooperative and concentrated man ner. On Demand.

courses.subject: NSCI
courses.title: Laboratory Practicum
courses.description: This course is designed specifically for students seeking teacher certification in one of the natural science fields. It is designed to enable them to plan, create and execute a laboratory in secondary school science courses. On Demand.

courses.subject: NSCI
courses.title: Health Professions Application Seminar
courses.description: This advanced seminar course supports students applying to health professions graduate programs. The seminar covers the application process, application timeline development, personal statement development, and interview preparation. Prerequisites: Permiss ion of instructor; junior standing recommended. Fall.
courses.prereq_text: Permiss ion of instructor; junior standing recommended
prereq_other: Permiss ion of instructor; junior standing recommended

courses.subject: NSCI
courses.title: Medical Terminology
courses.description: A programmed course designed to meet objectives related to career goals in biological and health -related fields such as medical secretary, social worker, or records clerk. Fall, Spring, Winter.

courses.subject: NSCI
courses.title: Special Topics in Natural Science
courses.description: A variable topics seminar course at the senior level in the environmental and natural sciences. On Demand.
