courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Introduction to Philosophy
courses.description: A study of the basic concerns of philosophy which seeks to introduce the student to the spirit of reasoned inquiry and to encourage a reflective approach to life. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Logic
courses.description: An introduction to critical thinking and traditional logic including argument analysis, fallacies, and basic symbolic logic. Spring.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: The Good Life
courses.description: A study of philosophical, religious, and cultural perspectives on the meaning of life and how to live well. Spring of even-numbered years.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Ancient and Medieval Philosophy
courses.description: A study of the ideas and arguments of major philosophers from ancient Greece through the Middle Ages. Prerequisite: PHIL 1003 or permission of instructor. On Demand.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Western Political Thought I
courses.description: As a systematic intellectual enterprise, theories of political philosophy address perennial problems of political relations. This course is an intensive analysis of the principal political theorists in the Western tradition from Plato through Machiavelli. Primary emphasis on their texts is complemented by consideration of the historical contexts within which they wrote. Also listed as PSCI 3053. On Demand.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Western Political Thought II
courses.description: As a systematic intellectual enterprise, theories of political philosophy address perennial problems of political relations. This course is an intensive analysis of the principal political theorists in the Western tradition extending from Hobbes onward. Primary emphasis on their texts is complemented by consideration of the historical contexts within which they wrote. Also listed as PSCI 3063. On Demand.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Death and Dying
courses.description: A study of the role of death in human experience, including historical and cultural views of death and afterlife, the nature of grief, and ethical issues related to death and dying. Spring.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Issues in Science and Religion
courses.description: A study of the processes and products of theological reflection and scientific inquiry and issues that arise in the interaction of the two enterprises. This course satisfies the Scientific Connections requirement. Also listed as NSCI 3183. Fall of even-numbered years.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Suffering, Tragedy, and Christian Faith
courses.description: A study of the problems that suffering and tragedy raise for Christian faith. Topics include divine hiddenness, human cruelty, horrendous evils, natural disasters, animal suffering, and hell. Spring of odd-numbered years.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Christian Apologetics
courses.description: This course studies the Christian faith as a comprehensive world view. Special attention is paid to Christian responses to secular objections and competing world views. On Demand.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Modern and Contemporary Philosophy
courses.description: A study of major philosophers and philosophical movements from the Renaissance through the 20th Century. Prerequisite: PHIL 1003 or permission of instructor. Fall of odd-numbered years.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Christian Ethics
courses.description: A study of ethical analysis and decision-making within the context of a Christian world view. [CW3] Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophy of Religion
courses.description: A study of the philosophy of religion, its method and the philosophical issues related to religious commitment. On Demand.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Special Studies in Philosophy
courses.description: Prerequisite: Permission of the Chair of the Department of Philosophy and the Dean of the Pruet School of Christian Studies. On Demand.
courses.prereq_text: Permission of the Chair of the Department of Philosophy and the Dean of the Pruet School of Christian Studies
prereq_other: Permission of the Chair of the Department of Philosophy and the Dean of the Pruet School of Christian Studies

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Engineering Graphics
courses.description: An introduction to engineering design and the related graphical tools used to communicate design concepts. Drawings will be created by hand and on computer using projections such as orthographic, isometric, and auxiliary. Lecture one hour, lab two hours p er week. Spring.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Introduction to Physics and Engineering
courses.description: An introduction to the fields of Physics and Engineering designed to introduce students to the wide variety of career paths available and the skills necessary to work in a particular field. Discussion on practical topics such as engineering failures and et hics will also be included. Fall.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Astronomy
courses.description: An introduction to basic stellar astronomy including a study of the planets, earth-moon-sun relationships, stars, and galaxies; the history of astronomy, and contemporary theories and observations. On Demand.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: College Physics I
courses.description: Introductory non-calculus-based course in the fundamental principles of physics including 1D and 2D mechanics, fluids, and waves. Lecture three hours, laboratory two hours per week. Prerequisite: MATH 1003 or equivalent and proficiency in trigonometry. Fall.
courses.prereq_text: MATH 1003 or equivalent and proficiency in trigonometry

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: College Physics II
courses.description: Introductory non-calculus-based course in the fundamental principles of physics including electricity and magnetism, basic electric circuits, and optics. Lecture three hours, laboratory two hours per week. Prerequisite: PHYS 2024 and MATH 1003 or equivalen t and proficiency in trigonometry. Spring.
courses.prereq_text: PHYS 2024 and MATH 1003 or equivalen t and proficiency in trigonometry

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: University Physics I
courses.description: Introductory course in physics using calculus, designed for physical science and engineering majors. This course will focus on topics in Mechanics. Lecture three hours, laboratory two hours per week. Corequisite MATH 2014. Spring.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: University Physics II
courses.description: Introductory course in physics using calculus, designed for physical science and engineering majors. This course to focus on a survey of Electricity and Magnetism. Lecture three hours, laboratory two hours per week. Prerequisite PHYS 2054 or PHYS 2024 and MATH 2014. Fall.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: University Physics III
courses.description: Introductory course in physics using calculus, designed for physical science, education, and engineering majors. This course will focus specifically on topics in oscillations and mechanical waves, thermodynamics, light and optics. Prerequisite: PHYS 2024 and MATH 2014 or PHYS 2054 Spring.
courses.prereq_text: PHYS 2024 and MATH 2014 or PHYS 2054 Spring.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Special Topics in Physics
courses.description: A course varied to meet the needs of the department. On Demand.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Statics
courses.description: Equilibrium states are studied by analyzing the forces and torques on both two - and three-dimensional rigid bodies. Topics include structural analysis, internal forces, and friction. Prerequisites: Either PHYS 2054 or both PHYS 2024 and MATH 2014. Fall.
courses.prereq_text: Either PHYS 2054 or both PHYS 2024 and MATH 2014

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Dynamics
courses.description: A study of the kinematics and kinetics of a particle and of rigid bodies in two and three dimensions. Analysis will include force, energy, and momentum methods. Prerequisite: PHYS 2123. Spring.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Introduction to Modern Physics
courses.description: An introduction to the basic principles of 20 th-century physics. Topics typically include special relativity, particle properties of electromagnetic radiation, wave properties of particles, the uncertainty principle, and atomic spectra. Lecture three hours, laboratory three hours per week. Prerequisites: Either PHYS 2064 or both PHYS 2034 and MATH 2014. [CW3] Fall.
courses.prereq_text: Either PHYS 2064 or both PHYS 2034 and MATH 2014

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Thermodynamics
courses.description: A study of the basic principles of classical thermodynamics and statistical mechanics including thermal equilibrium; first, s econd, and third laws of thermodynamics; entropy; partition functions; and statistical ensembles. Applications to engines, refriger ators and others will be considered. Prerequisites: PHYS 2064 or both PHYS 2034 and MATH 2014. Spring.
courses.prereq_text: PHYS 2064 or both PHYS 2034 and MATH 2014

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Electricity and Magnetism I
courses.description: A study of the principles of electricity and magnetism in a vacuum. Topics typically include electrostatics, magnetostatics, Laplace’s Equation, Maxwell’s Equations, and conservation laws. Vector Calculus is introduced and used throughout. Lecture three hours, laboratory three hours per week. Prerequisites: PHYS 2034 or 2064; MATH 3034. Spring of even-numbered years.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Intermediate Physics Laboratory
courses.description: This course is designed to further a student’s education in experimental physics. The student will become familiar with more advanced equipment and techniques, more sophisticated mathematical tools to analyze the data, and then use them to perform several experiments in a variety of fields. Prerequisite: PHYS 3004. On Demand.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Biophysics Seminar
courses.description: This seminar will expose students to current topics in biophysics. Prerequisite: PHYS 2034 or PHYS 2064. On Demand.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Electrical Circuits
courses.description: An introduction to the fundamental concepts of electrical circuits, including circuit variables, elements, and simple resisti ve circuits; circuit laws and network theorems; op-amps; inductance; capacitance; natural and step responses of RL, RC, and RLC circuits. Lecture three hours, laboratory three hours per week. Prerequisites: Either PHYS 2064 or both PHYS 2034 and MATH 2014. Fall of odd - numbered years.
courses.prereq_text: Either PHYS 2064 or both PHYS 2034 and MATH 2014

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Mechanics of Materials
courses.description: Stress and strain in structural members subjected to tension, compression, torsion, and bending, and the design of these members. Analysis and basic design of columns and of statically determinate and indeterminate structural members. Simple structural member connections. Prerequisite: ENGR 2123. Spring.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Internship
courses.description: Internships must relate to the emphasis of the student’s coursework (lab or field) and must be approved in advance by the Department Chair and the Dean of Natural Sciences. The course will be graded on a Satisfactory-Unsatisfactory basis where Satisfactory is defined as a grade of C or higher. A limit of three hours of internship credit may be applied to the requirements for a degree. On Demand.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Classical Mechanics I
courses.description: A study of the fundamentals of mechanics, including Newtonian dynamics and conservation laws, oscillations, central force motion, the calculus of variations, generalized coordinates, Lagrangian dynamics, and Hamiltonian dynamics. Prerequisites: PHYS 2024 o r 2054; MATH 3034. Fall of odd-numbered years.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Senior Laboratory
courses.description: Experiments in thermometry, solid state, atomic and molecular physics. Open only to Senior Physics students. On Demand.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Introduction to Quantum Mechanics
courses.description: An introduction to the concepts and formalism of quantum mechanics. The focus will be the time -independent Schrödinger equation and its application to systems such as the harmonic oscillator, square -well potentials, and the hydrogen atom. Prerequisite: P HYS 3004; Corequisite: MATH 3043. Spring of odd-numbered years.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Mathematical Physics
courses.description: A selection of topics in applied mathematics of interest to scientists and engineers. Topics include vector calculus, complex numbers, variables and functions, Fourier series, and special functions defined by solutions to differential equations. Prerequisites: PHYS 2034 or 2064; MATH 3034. On Demand.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Introduction to Physics Research
courses.description: To introduce the student to the theory, techniques and methods of laboratory and library research within the broader liberal arts experience students gained through the Ouachita Core. Open only to Senior Physics students, or by permission of instructor. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Electricity and Magnetism II
courses.description: A continuation of PHYS 3033 with a focus on electromagnetic fields in matter, electromagnetic waves, radiation, and applicati ons in relativity. Prerequisite: PHYS 3033. On Demand.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Classical Mechanics II
courses.description: A continuation of PHYS 4003 with a focus on rigid bodies, scattering, nonlinear oscillations, coupled oscillations, moving coordinate systems, and continuous media. Prerequisite: PHYS 4003; MATH 3043. On Demand.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Laboratory Peer Instructor
courses.description: Student peer instructors will assist the faculty in laboratory or lecture courses. Peer instructors will engage in individual and small group instruction during laboratory or course review sessions, will be prepared to answer questions related to weekly lab or course exercises, and may assist in the preparation, administration, and grading assignments. Student peer instructors may be required to desig n a laboratory…

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Introduction to Quantum Mechanics II
courses.description: A continuation of PHYS 4043 including applications and approximation methods in quantum mechanics as well as the time -dependent Schrödinger equation. Prerequisite: PHYS 4043. On Demand.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Physics Education Proficiency
courses.description: The course is designed to help students prepare for the Praxis II exam in physics. Students will review physics concepts learned during their physics education course of study with topics related to the Praxis exam. Spring.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Senior Capstone Experience
courses.description: This course will integrate knowledge and skills from physics with the broader liberal arts experience students gain through the Ouachita Core. Students will engage in elements of professional preparation in addition to participating in an exit exam. Open only to senior Physics students, or by permission of instructor. May not be counted toward a minor. On Demand.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Medical Physics
courses.description: A study of the application of basic physics principles to the workings of the body and medical instrumentation. Prerequisites: BIOL 2024 and either PHYS 2034 or PHYS 2064. Spring of even-numbered years. 4701-4. Special Topics in Physics. A course varied to meet the needs of the department. On Demand.
courses.prereq_text: BIOL 2024 and either PHYS 2034 or PHYS 2064

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Individual Study, Group Study, Research
courses.description: This course is offered to provide competent students with an opportu nity to do independent study and research or to study special topics. On Demand. SCHOOL OF PERFORMING ARTS

courses.subject: PSCI
courses.title: Introduction to Politics
courses.description: An introduction to the study of politics and the discipline of Political Science, focusing on individual, collective and inst itutional political behavior. On Demand.

courses.subject: PSCI
courses.title: Comparative Politics
courses.description: A survey of concepts, approaches and methodologies for theory-building in comparing political systems. Fall.

courses.subject: PSCI
courses.title: State and Local Government and Politics
courses.description: An introduction to formal and informal political institutions at both the state and local level, including a student simulati on of political choices and behavior. On Demand.

courses.subject: PSCI
courses.title: American National Government
courses.description: This course explores the structure and dynamics of American national government, providing a broad -based introduction to the ideas and institutions that shape politics in the contemporary United States: The Constitution, federalism, Congress, the presidency, the judiciary, bureaucracy, political parties, elections, participation, the media, and public opinion. By cultivating a deeper understanding of how government…

courses.subject: PSCI
courses.title: Philosophy and Methods of Political Science
courses.description: A consideration of the philosophy and research methods of Political Science for students who have had no previous training in statistics and only a normal high school mathematical background. Fall.

courses.subject: PSCI
courses.title: Arkansas Government and Politics
courses.description: An institutional and behavioral analysis of Arkansas government and politics. Spring of odd-numbered years.

courses.subject: PSCI
courses.title: World Politics
courses.description: An introduction to the study of how countries as well as other international actors interact with each other. [CW2] Spring.

courses.subject: PSCI
courses.title: Constitutional Law
courses.description: A case method analysis of landmark Supreme Court decisions addressing institutional conflict, basic criminal rights and proce dures, first amendment freedoms, the fourteenth amendment and federalism. Spring of odd-numbered years.

courses.subject: PSCI
courses.title: The Judicial Process
courses.description: A consideration of various theories explaining judicial decision -making, the political impact of these decisions, court structures and procedures, and the politics of judicial selection. Spring of even-numbered years.

courses.subject: PSCI
courses.title: Western Political Thought I
courses.description: As a systematic intellectual enterprise, theories of political philosophy address perennial problems of political relations. This course is an intensive analysis of the principal political theorists in the Western tradition from Plato through Machiavelli. Primary emphasis on their texts is complemented by consideration of the historical contexts within which they wrote. Also listed as PHIL 3053. [CW3] On Demand.

courses.subject: PSCI
courses.title: Western Political Thought II
courses.description: As a systematic intellectual enterprise, theories of political philosophy address perennial problems of political relations. This course is an intensive analysis of the principal political theorists in the Western tradition extending from Hobbes onward. Primary emphasis on their texts is complemented by consideration of the historical contexts within which they wrote. Also listed as PHIL 3063. [CW3] On Demand. 1 Hebe…

courses.subject: PSCI
courses.title: Washington Seminar
courses.description: A learning experience in Washington, D.C. that explores the American national political institutions and processes covered in PSCI 3070. Prerequisite: PSCI 3070. Winter of odd-numbered years.

courses.subject: PSCI
courses.title: Model U
courses.description: N. Seminar. Students study the issues and procedures of the United Nations. Prerequisite: permission of the instructor is required. Also listed as HIST 3080 and INTL 3080. Fall.
courses.prereq_text: permission of the instructor is required
prereq_other: permission of the instructor is required

courses.subject: PSCI
courses.title: Model U
courses.description: N. with Practicum. Students prepare for a regional simulation of the United Nations by learning about their country’s history, government, and foreign policy. Students enroll for this only if this is their first time attending a Model U. N. simulation as a Ouachita student. Prerequisite: permission of the instructor and HIST/INTL/PSCI 3080. Also listed as HIST 3083 and INTL 3083. Spring.
courses.prereq_text: permission of the instructor and HIST/INTL/PSCI 3080
prereq_other: permission of the instructor and HIST/INTL/PSCI 3080

courses.subject: PSCI
courses.title: Model U
courses.description: N. Practicum. Students prepare for a regional simulation of the United Nations by learning about their country’s history, government, and foreign policy. This course cannot be in the same department that HIST/INTL/PSCI 3083 was taken. Prerequisite: permission of the ins tructor and HIST/INTL/PSCI 3083. Also listed as HIST 3091 and INTL 3091. Spring.
courses.prereq_text: permission of the ins tructor and HIST/INTL/PSCI 3083
prereq_other: permission of the ins tructor and HIST/INTL/PSCI 3083

courses.subject: PSCI
courses.title: Criminal Procedure
courses.description: A survey of constitutional law governing criminal procedure from arrest to trial, including right to counsel, arrest, searche s, electronic surveillance, entrapment, interrogation and confession, pre -trial identification procedures, grand jury investigation s, and witness preparation and conduct. Fall of odd-numbered years.

courses.subject: PSCI
courses.title: Parties, Campaigns and Elections
courses.description: An examination of the place of political parties in the study of politics, with a heavy emphasis on American parties, their role in electoral politics, the conduct of election campaigns and the meaning of elections. Spring of even-numbered years.

courses.subject: PSCI
courses.title: American Political Thought
courses.description: A critical consideration of the origins, development , and content of American political thought, emphasizing the expressions of major political actors and the interpretations given to fundamental political concepts. On Demand.

courses.subject: PSCI
courses.title: Public Policy
courses.description: An analysis of the formulation, making and content of American domestic public policies, acquainting students with salient is sues on the policy agenda. Spring of even-numbered years alternating with PSCI 4043.

courses.subject: PSCI
courses.title: Public Administration
courses.description: An in -depth seminar in the theory and behavior of large social organizations, specifically bureaucracies, focusing on the national government’s administration of public policy. Spring of even-numbered years alternating with PSCI 4033.

courses.subject: PSCI
courses.title: American Diplomacy
courses.description: A study of foreign policy in the United States in fact and theory, analyzing America’s involvement in World Affairs from 1776 to the present. Current diplomatic policy of the United States is examined in relation to the past. Also listed as HIST 4053. Fall of odd - numbered years.

courses.subject: PSCI
courses.title: European Politics
courses.description: A study of the political institutions, policies, and major changes occurring in the region. Fall of even-numbered years.

courses.subject: PSCI
courses.title: The American Congress
courses.description: A consideration of the evolution, organizational structures, functions and processes of the contemporary American Congress an d its place in the American political system. Fall of odd-numbered years.

courses.subject: PSCI
courses.title: The American Presidency
courses.description: An inquiry into the evolution, organizational structure and operation of the contemporary American presidency, focusing on th e relationship between the president and the political environment. Fall of even-numbered years.

courses.subject: PSCI
courses.title: International Law and Organization
courses.description: This course examines the role of international law and the activities and effects of intergovernmental organizations as well as non- governmental organizations. Spring of even-numbered years.

courses.subject: PSCI
courses.title: Politics of the Global South
courses.description: A substantive and theoretical study of the political processes and major issues confronting Latin America, Africa, and Centra l and Southern Asia. Spring of odd-numbered years.

courses.subject: PSCI
courses.title: Topical Seminar
courses.description: The course covers unique and timely topics in Political Science. Because a different topic will be offered each semester, the course may be repeated once for credit. Prerequisite: Approval of the instructor. [CW3] Spring.

courses.subject: PSCI
courses.title: Special Studies in Political Science
courses.description: Directed research in Political Science. Admission by consent of the instructor. On Demand.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: General Psychology
courses.description: An introductory course dealing with elementary principles, terminology, and various aspects of different branches of the subject. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Human Development
courses.description: A survey of human development from conception to death. Physical, cognitive, and social process and how they affect human development will be emphasized. Prerequisite: PSYC 1013. Spring.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Statistics
courses.description: A course in descriptive and inferential statistical techniques with emphasis on analysis of experimental data. Both manual and computer procedures will be covered. Fall.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Research Methods I
courses.description: The basic principles involved, and the techniques used in experimentation and non -experimental research, including hypothesis generation, design, data collection, and scientific writing. Prerequisites: PSYC 1013. Co-requisite: PSYC 2054. Fall.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Social Psychology
courses.description: A survey of research and theory in social psychology. Topics include the self, person perception, attitudes, culture, conform ity, persuasion, group behavior, prejudice, aggression, and close relationships. Also listed as SOCI 3013. Fall.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Behavior Analysis
courses.description: A study of the principles and theories of learning in the field of behavior analysis. This course will cover basic learning principles, common behavioral procedures, the research methods and techniques of behavior analysis, as well as the application of b ehavior analysis across a wide range of populations, settings, and behaviors. Prerequisite: PSYC 1013. On Demand.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Research Methods II
courses.description: Application of the basic principles of research design, with an emphasis on research ethics and scientific writing. Each stud ent will design and complete a research project. Prerequisite: PSYC 2063. Spring.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Neuroscience
courses.description: An introduction to the biological substrate of behavior and experience, especially as expressed in neuroanatomy, neurophysiology and behavioral neuroscience. Prerequisite: CORE 2334 or BIOL 1014. Spring.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Psychometrics
courses.description: An introduction to the basic theories and principles behind the development and use of tests and measurements of psychologica l constructs. Prerequisites: PSYC 1013, 2054. On Demand.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Abnormal Psychology
courses.description: A study of mental and emotional deviations and illnesses. Consideration is given to the incidence, causes, symptoms, dynamics , prognosis, and theories of treatment of various conditions. Prerequisite: PSYC 1013. Spring.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Personality
courses.description: A survey of research and theory in personality psychology, linking current research with important personality approaches, in cluding trait, cognitive, learning, cultural, and psychodynamic theories. Prerequisite: PSYC 1013. Spring.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Health Psychology
courses.description: A course investigating how biological, social, and psychological factors influence health and illness. Key emphases will be b ehavioral medicine, illness prevention, rehabilitation, pain management, and the intersection of stress with physical health. On Demand.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Mental Health Issues in Law Enforcement
courses.description: This course surveys the relationship of mental illness to crime. Topics include the nature, prevalence, and consequences of mental disorder, substance use, and violence among criminal offenders; violence risk assessment; compassionate response and communication; and the institutional treatment and rehabilitation of mentally ill offenders. Additionally, this course will review the psychological effects of secondary tr…

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: History of Psychology
courses.description: An historical survey of the development of psychology within intellectual and socio -cultural contexts. Prerequisite: Six Junior -Senior hours in Psychology. Fall.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Counseling Psychology
courses.description: An introduction to clinical psychology as represented by selected contemporary approaches. Prerequisites: PSYC 1013; PSYC 3093, 3103 recommended. Fall.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Cognition
courses.description: A study of the basic mental operations that support our ability to obtain and use information, such as memory, attention, and perception. Prerequisite: PSYC 1013. Fall.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Senior Research
courses.description: A course designed to give the student additional experience in conducting individualized psychological experimentation. A stu dent cannot earn credit for more than 3 hours total. Prerequisite: PSYC 3053. On Demand.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Meta-Analysis
courses.description: An introduction to meta-analysis and systematic review. Includes basic meta-analytic design and implementation, statistical models and publication bias, and interpretation and presentation of results. Prerequisite: A grade of C or better in PSYC 2054 and PSYC 2063. On Demand.
courses.prereq_text: A grade of C or better in PSYC 2054 and PSYC 2063

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Advanced Statistics
courses.description: A deep dive into statistical analyses commonly used in the social sciences including analysis of variance, repeated measures, regression, analysis of covariance, and multivariate analysis of variance. Prerequisites: A grade of C or better in PSYC 2054 . On Demand.
courses.prereq_text: A grade of C or better in PSYC 2054 . On Demand.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Peer Instructor
courses.description: Student peer instructors will be assigned to a psychology course to help facilitate student learning. The course, which may be taken up to two times, is graded S/U. Prerequisite: Junior or Senior standing and instructor permission. On Demand.
courses.prereq_text: Junior or Senior standing and instructor permission
prereq_other: Junior or Senior standing and instructor permission

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Psychology Internship
courses.description: This course provides students with the opportunity to receive academic credit for supervised, professional level service and work experience. Prerequisites: PSYC 1013, Junior or Senior standing, and instructor permission. On Demand.
courses.prereq_text: PSYC 1013, Junior or Senior standing, and instructor permission
prereq_other: PSYC 1013, Junior or Senior standing, and instructor permission

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Topical Seminar
courses.description: This course examines a specialized domain of psychology not covered in the department's general course offerings. Students wi ll explore a variety of primary and secondary sources. Because topics vary, a student may take up to three different topics for credit. Prerequisite: PSYC 1013 and junior or senior standing. [CW3] Fall, Spring.
courses.prereq_text: PSYC 1013 and junior or senior standing

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Special Studies in Psychology
courses.description: A course designed to broaden the student’s psychological knowledge through directed study or research. Prerequisites: Junior or Senior standing, and instructor’s permission. On Demand.
courses.prereq_text: Junior or Senior standing, and instructor’s permission
prereq_other: Junior or Senior standing, and instructor’s permission

courses.subject: SCED
courses.title: Secondary Methods and Classroom Management
courses.description: A study of resources and methods of motivating students and directing learning. It includes the study of selected teaching approaches including individualized education programs. Prerequisite: EDFN 2003. Spring.

courses.subject: SCED
courses.title: The Secondary School Curriculum
courses.description: A course in principles and practices in the organization and development of the curriculum for the secondary school. The course includes a study of content, purposes, and objectives of the secondary school curriculum. Pre-requisite: Admission to Teacher Education. On Demand.

courses.subject: SCED
courses.title: Special Studies in Education
courses.description: Provides advanced students with an opportunity to pursue independent study on significant education problems. On Demand.

courses.subject: SCED
courses.title: Contemporary Problems in American Education
courses.description: A workshop concerned with the problems of compensatory education and current issues. On Demand.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Introduction to Sociology
courses.description: This course introduces basic principles in understanding patterns of social relations–including theoretical perspectives and sociological methods–while examining major societal institutions. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Introduction to Social Services
courses.description: This course surveys social services available in American society, past and present, as well as reasons for these services ra ther than others. Coverage includes the skills and perspectives required in effectively administered social services. On Demand.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Statistics in Social Sciences
courses.description: This course examines the conceptual basis and application of statistical analysis in the social sciences, including descriptive statistics, the logic of hypothesis-testing and inferential statistics, correlation and regression, analysis of variance, matched-subjects designs, and non-parametric procedures. Fall.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Race, Class, and Gender
courses.description: This course will survey a comprehensive range of theories and research on race, class, and gender inequalities. Students will explore the intersection of these concepts and how they shape society, individual life chances, and daily social interactions. Fall.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Geospatial Data Analysis
courses.description: Geospatial analysis is the gathering, display, and manipulation of imagery, GPS, satellite, and historical data, described geographically. Students will learn the tools, methods, and software necessary to manage and analyze spatial data and information to be applied within their own disciplines. Fall of even-numbered years.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Social Psychology
courses.description: A survey of research and theory in social psychology. Topics include the self, person perception, attitudes, culture, conformity, persuasion, group behavior, prejudice, aggression, and close relationships. Also listed as PSYC 3013. Fall.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Sociology of the Family
courses.description: This course studies the family as a social institution and as a unique small group, examining theoretical and empirical research related to mate selection, marital interaction, and child socialization. Topics include contemporary demographic trends and cu ltural practices. Fall.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Sociology of the Community
courses.description: This course investigates a sociological analysis of human life in urban, suburban, and rural society, focusing on changes in relationships and community. Introduces students to GIS mapping. Prerequisite: SOCI 1003, or instructor approval. Spring.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Social Science Research Methods
courses.description: This course examines concepts and methods used in sociology, criminal justice, and social work to research community needs as well as to evaluate interventions and program effectiveness. Both quantitative and qualitative models receive emphasis. Prerequisite: SOCI 1003 and SOCI 2034. Spring.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Crime and Deviance
courses.description: This course explores criminal and deviant behaviors such as alcohol abuse, illicit drug use, mental disorder, crime, law -enforcement, deviance, and prostitution, focusing on social definitions and causal explanations. Prerequisite: SOCI 1003 or CJUS 3023 Criminology. Also listed as CJUS 3123. Fall.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Sociology Internship
courses.description: An internship with an approved law enforcement agency, court, or affiliated entity. Minimum 50-hour work requirement. Cross-listed as CJUS 4023 Criminal Justice Internship. Fall, Summer, Spring.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Classical Sociological Theory
courses.description: This course explores the major theoretical issues raised by classical theorists such as Weber, Simmel, Marx, Durkheim, and Me ad as well as their influence on contemporary theory. Spring.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Medical Sociology
courses.description: This course studies the development of medicine as a profession and as a social institution, including medicine’s place withi n the structure of society and its relationship to demographic shifts and social change. Also receiving attention is how social class relates to health and healthcare disparities. Spring.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Topical Seminar
courses.description: This course examines a focused domain of sociology not covered in the department’s general course offerings. Students will explore a variety of primary and secondary sources. Because topics vary, a student may take up to three different topics for credit. Prerequisite: SOCI 1003 and Junior or Senior standing. Fall, Spring.
courses.prereq_text: SOCI 1003 and Junior or Senior standing

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Applied Sociology Capstone Seminar
courses.description: This course provides students the opportunity to reflect on the discipline of sociology, their experience within the discipli ne, and the application of sociological thought in understanding the world. Students will also reflect on how their faith and sociological perspectives intersect in developing an understanding of human life. Senior-standing required. [CW3] Spring.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Special Studies in Sociology
courses.description: A directed program of study to meet specific needs and interests of the individual. On Demand.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Elementary Spanish I in México
courses.description: A course in the fundamentals of grammar and composition, using the conversational approach. Readings on elementary level stimulate interest in Hispanic culture. The course will involve a travel component; the course will incur an additional course fee. Co-requisite: HIST 2103 Latin American History. On Demand.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Elementary Spanish II in México
courses.description: A course in the fundamentals of grammar and composition, using the conversational approach. Readings on elementary level stimulate interest in Hispanic culture. The course will involve a travel component; the course will incur an additional course fee. Co-requisite: HIST 2103 Latin American History. On Demand.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Intermediate
courses.description: Spanish I A review of basic grammar and a study of in -depth grammar with practice in reading, writing, listening and conversation Prerequisite: SPAN 1023 or consent of instructor. Fall.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Intermediate Spanish II
courses.description: A study of in -depth grammar in the context of written compositions and oral presentations. Prerequisite: SPAN 2033 or consent of instructor. Spring.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Intermediate Spanish I in México
courses.description: A review of basic grammar and a study of in-depth grammar with practice in reading, writing, listening and conversation. The course will involve a travel component; the course will incur an additional course fee. Co-requisite: HIST 2103 Latin American History. On Demand.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Intermediate Spanish II in México
courses.description: A study of in -depth grammar in the context of written compositions and oral presentations. Prerequisite: SPAN 2033 or consent of instructor. The course will incur an additional course fee. Co-requisite: HIST 2103 Latin American History. On Demand.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Cultural Conversations
courses.description: Training in the art of composition and in diction and conversation for students wishing to acquire fluency in the spoken lang uage. Prerequisite: SPAN 2043 or consent of instructor. Fall.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Written Expressions
courses.description: Designed to give training in elements of advanced grammar, including contextualized work in compositions and written exercise s Prerequisite: SPAN 2043 or consent of instructor. [CW2] Fall.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Peer Instructor
courses.description: Student peer instructors will be assigned to a SPAN 1013 or 1023 sections to facilitate student learning and work with students to help them become more confident speakers and writers of Spanish. A total of 1.5 work hours per week is expected. The course, which may be taken two times, is graded S/U. Students must receive instructor’s permission to enroll each semester. On demand.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Internship
courses.description: With a variety of opportunities to use Spanish in our community, this internship enables students to gain hands -on experience for academic credit and resume-building. The student is responsible for initiating the internship and getting approval through the university. On demand.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Topical Seminar
courses.description: This seminar will vary by semester, with one of the following titles listed: (1) Literature (fiction, poetry, and/or nonfiction of any historical period or geographical region); (2) Linguistics (phonology, syntax, semantics, or any other topic related to linguistics); (3) Culture (film, drama, literature, photography, translations, or other interdisciplinary topics). [CW3] Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Civilizations of the Spanish Speaking World
courses.description: Students will study the history, culture, and geography of Spain, Latin America, and Hispanics in the USA as reflected in art istic production and political thought. Prerequisites: SPAN 3123 and SPAN 3133, or consent of instructor. Spring.
courses.prereq_text: SPAN 3123 and SPAN 3133, or consent of instructor
prereq_other: SPAN 3123 and SPAN 3133, or consent of instructor

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Methods of Teaching Spanish
courses.description: A study of modern methodology of foreign language teaching. Students will take the Praxis II World Spanish and Oral Proficiency Interview as a part of the course. Prerequisite: Consent of instructor. On Demand.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Culture and Literature of México (Taught in México)
courses.description: Accompanying a study abroad experience in Mexico, this course will cover topics in Latin American literature and language. Representative texts from Latin America will be examined from various critical perspectives, placing special emphasis on the literature of the place where the course takes place. The course will incur an additional course fee. Co -requisite: HIST 2103 Latin American History. On Demand.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Seminar in Values and Vocation
courses.description: Students explore the meanings and limits of work; they will explore and articulate the value of their studies in languages and literature; and they will prepare for professional careers and/or graduate studies. Also listed as ENGL 4601. Fall.

courses.subject: SPAN
courses.title: Special Courses in Spanish
courses.description: Special topics and individual studies based on the needs and interests of students. On Demand.

courses.subject: SPED
courses.title: Teaching Exceptional Learners
courses.description: This course is a “Special Education 101 Academy”, which emphasizes the importance of the least restrictive environment for all students while reviewing the law and responsibilities of all stakeholders involved in the student’s learning. Prerequisite: Admission to Teacher Education or permission by the dean. (Cross-listed as EDFN 3083 Teaching Exceptional Learners). Spring.
courses.prereq_text: Admission to Teacher Education or permission by the dean.

courses.subject: SPED
courses.title: Classroom and Behavior Management
courses.description: This course will focus on strategies to ensure students are provided with the appropriate accommodations and interventions to ensure student success. Prerequisite: Admission to Teacher Education or permission from the dean. Spring.
courses.prereq_text: Admission to Teacher Education or permission from the dean.

courses.subject: SPED
courses.title: Assessment and Differentiation of Diverse Learners
courses.description: This course will focus on the evaluation process for students with exceptionalities as well interpreting the data to differentiate based on the students’ needs. Prerequisite: Admission to Teacher Education; SPED 3083 and SPED 3093 or permission from the Dean. Fall.
courses.prereq_text: Admission to Teacher Education; SPED 3083 and SPED 3093 or permission from the Dean.

courses.subject: SPED
courses.title: Instructional Programming for Diverse Learners
courses.description: This course will focus on the needs of each student to determine individualization of instruction. Prerequisite: Admission to Teacher Education; SPED 3083, SPED 3093 or permission from the Dean. Fall.
courses.prereq_text: Admission to Teacher Education; SPED 3083, SPED 3093 or permission from the Dean.

courses.subject: SPTM
courses.title: Big Data/Data Mining
courses.description: An introduction to the concepts of Big Data and methods of Data Mining. Subject content includes sports, politics, finance, marketing, psychology, and climate. Fall.

courses.subject: SPTM
courses.title: Sport Law
courses.description: The legal environment specific to the business of sport, including liability, contracts, and agencies. Spring.

courses.subject: SPTM
courses.title: Special Studies in Sport Management
courses.description: Given on demand and varied to meet the needs of seniors. On Demand.

courses.subject: SPTM
courses.title: Sport Management Internship
courses.description: This class is an applied integrative experience in which students will be placed under a mentor in the field outside the university setting. These will generally be 400 hours in length. Summer, On Demand. CHESLEY AND ELIZABETH PRUET SCHOOL OF CHRISTIAN STUDIES Associate Professor Jeremy Greer, Dean

courses.subject: SSCI
courses.title: Special Methods in Social Studies
courses.description: A course designed to provide theory and methodology in secondary social studies teaching. It emphasizes the use of the unit plan and problem approaches in teaching social studies and in providing learning. Prerequisite: EDFN 2003. Fall of odd-numbered years.

courses.subject: SSCI
courses.title: Senior Seminar
courses.description: This seminar encourages students to integrate knowledge and skills from their major field of study with the broader liberal -arts experience provided by the Ouachita Core Curriculum. The course provides a basis for life-long learning, meaningful work, and service to humans in a diverse and interconnected world. Fall, Spring. 4951-6. Workshop. Provides upper division students an opportunity to approach current topics…

courses.subject: THDA
courses.title: Ballet
courses.description: Fundamentals of classical ballet technique, including barre, centre floor, and locomotor movement. Fall of odd-numbered years.

courses.subject: THDA
courses.title: Jazz 1
courses.description: Fundamentals of modern Jazz dance, including coordination, rhythm, and isolation. Spring of even-numbered years.

courses.subject: THDA
courses.title: Jazz 2
courses.description: Continued study of Jazz dance, including coordination, rhythm, and isolation. Spring of odd-numbered years.

courses.subject: THDA
courses.title: Modern Dance 1
courses.description: Fundamental of modern dance technique, including the development of strength, flexibility, balance, control, and endurance, w ith emphasis on proper body alignment. Fall of even-numbered years.

courses.subject: THDA
courses.title: Modern Dance 2
courses.description: Continued study in the fundamentals of modern dance technique, including development of strength, flexibility, balance, contr ol, and endurance, with emphasis on proper body alignment. Spring of odd-numbered years.

courses.subject: THDA
courses.title: Tap 1
courses.description: The study of tap dance on the elementary level through the development of flexibility, endurance, strength, kinesthetic aware ness, precision, and rhythm. Spring of even-numbered years.

courses.subject: THDA
courses.title: Tap 2
courses.description: Continued study of tap dance through the development of flexibility, endurance, strength, kinesthetic awareness, precision, and rhythm. Fall of even-numbered years.

courses.subject: THDA
courses.title: Musical Theatre Choreography
courses.description: A practical course that studies and applies the art of directing and choreographing musical numbers for a stage musical. Prer equisite: four completed hours of THDA courses, or consent of instructor. Fall of odd-numbered years.

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Introduction to the Theatre
courses.description: A course designed to introduce students to the foundations of theatre arts. Emphasis is on the practical application and exp erience of the artistry and cultural significance of the theatre. Fall.

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Theatre Practicum
courses.description: Performance and/or participation in the semester’s theatrical productions. Theatre Practicum may be repeated for a total of four hours. Prerequisite: THEA 1003 or consent of instructor. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Theatre Workshop
courses.description: A practical application in the basic skills of acting, movement, stagecraft, makeup, theatre directing and production. Member ship by audition or invitation. Enrolling in this course and Musical Theatre Workshop 1101 simultaneously is not permitted. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Acting 1
courses.description: A study of the production of standard American speech, kinesics (body language) and stage combat as it relates to character development. Prerequisite: THEA 1003 or consent of instructor. Spring.

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Musical Theatre Workshop
courses.description: A practical application in the basic skills of acting, movement, singing, stagecraft, makeup, musical theatre directing and p roduction. Admittance by audition or personal interview with the director. Double-listed as MUEN 1101. Spring.

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Acting 2
courses.description: The study and application of basic acting and improvisational techniques. Emphasis is on personal awareness and creative sel f- expression in character development. Prerequisite: THEA 1042 or consent of instructor. Spring.

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Fundamentals of Stagecraft
courses.description: An introduction to technical problems in the production of plays; scenery, lighting, sound, costuming and makeup. Fall.

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Fundamentals of Design
courses.description: An introduction to the philosophical, critical, and practical processes of design in theatre scenographic art. Prerequisite: THEA 2013 or consent of instructor. Spring.

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Sophomore Recital Preparation
courses.description: This non-credit course is designed to prepare BFA musical theatre majors for a 15 -minute barrier recital in the sophomore year. To be taken the semester in which the recital is to be performed.

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Acting 3
courses.description: Studies in the exploration of character development and performance as applied to chosen genres of dramatic literature. The focus of this course is the practical application of acting theories and techniques utilized in performance of period plays. Prereq uisite: THEA 2003. Fall.

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Stage Lighting
courses.description: and Sound A study of the factors governing lighting design and sound design as a means of artistic expression Prerequisite: THEA 2023 or consent of instructor. Spring of odd-numbered years.

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Stage Makeup
courses.description: A study of the purposes, principles, and materials of stage makeup. There will be intensive laboratory practices in its application. Fall.

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Scene Design
courses.description: A study of the elements of design and the application of general design principles. The course includes work on models, sketc hes, renderings and working drawings. Prerequisite: THEA 2023 or consent of instructor. Fall of even-numbered years.

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Costuming
courses.description: A study of the elements of costume design and the graphics interpretation of characters from plays. A practical exploration of the basic construction of stage costumes. Spring.

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Teaching Theatre in the K-12 Classroom
courses.description: A study of the methods and technique of teaching drama in the K-12 classroom. On Demand.

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: History and Literature of Musical Theatre
courses.description: A history of musical theatre with an emphasis on style and performance of representative literature. [CW2] Fall of even -numbered years.

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Motion Picture Script Development
courses.description: An introduction to the rules and techniques of screenwriting for film. Also listed as COMM 3643. On Demand.

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Auditioning
courses.description: Studies in the development of a repertory and techniques for auditions in music, drama, and dance with emphasis on the musical theatre audition. Prerequisite: THEA 2003. Fall.

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Senior Theatre Practicum
courses.description: A Senior theatre experience in an area of interest or expertise. This course allows the student to explore their creativity in areas of interest in the theatre and reflect on their pursuit of this area. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Theatre History 1
courses.description: An historical survey of the theatre from the Greek to the French Neo-Classical period. [CW2] Fall.

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Theatre History 2
courses.description: An historical survey of the theatre from the eighteenth century to the present. [CW3] Spring.

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Dramatic Theory and Play
courses.description: Development A practical and theoretical course designed to encourage the development of new and original works for the stage through a workshop environment The emphasis is on practical application of dramatic theory through analyzing existing works, writing new works , and producing final drafts in staged readings. Spring of even-numbered years.

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Acting 4
courses.description: Accelerated studies in scene work, styles, and/or acting approaches. Prerequisite THEA 3013. Spring.

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: American Drama
courses.description: An appraisal of the theatre in American society by the study of representative playwrights. Spring of odd-numbered years.

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Play Directing
courses.description: A course to acquaint the student through study and practice with the problems of producing plays. Prerequisites: THEA 2003 and THEA 2023. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Irene Ryan Audition Course
courses.description: A non-credit preparation course for students and their partners selected from the fall productions to be Irene Ryan Acting Scholars hip audition participants. Spring.

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Creative Drama for Classroom Teachers
courses.description: This course emphasizes the use of drama with and for children with an emphasis in oral interpretation. On Demand.

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Senior Recital Preparation
courses.description: This non-credit course is designed to prepare BFA musical theatre majors for a 50-minute barrier recital in the senior year. To be taken the semester in which the recital is to be performed.

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Motion Picture Production
courses.description: Narrative filmmaking with digital cinema gear, including a script breakdown, storyboarding, screen acting, directing, cinemat ography, coverage, and editing of a short film. The course may be repeated once for credit. Fall of odd-numbered years.

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Shakespeare
courses.description: This course examines the major plays of Shakespeare. Also listed as ENGL 4223. Fall of even-numbered years.

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Studies in Drama
courses.description: This variable topic course presents the chief movements and greatest plays of literature. Also listed as ENGL 4303. On Demand.

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Twentieth Century Theatre
courses.description: Selected areas of twentieth century theatre, including dramatic criticism. The course may be taken twice for credit providing that the topics are different. On Demand.

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Special Studies in Theatre Arts
courses.description: A course arranged to meet the needs of students concentrating in Theatre Arts. Independent study is possible in dramatic hist ory, theory, playwriting, production and the teaching of dramatics. On Demand.

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Special Studies in Technical Theatre
courses.description: A course designed to meet the needs of students concentrating in technical theatre. Independent study is possible in stage ma naging, properties construction, design of lighting, costumes, or sets. On Demand.

programs.name: Core Curriculum
programs.school: School of Interdisciplinary Studies
programs.source_text: The Ouachita Core. The three-part structure of the curriculum comprises the Common Core, the Flexible Core, and the Experiential Core. COMMON CORE (The following courses are required of all students, though in limited cases, introductory courses in the major may substitute for some required courses (see major requirements). Course descriptions are included below.): CORE 1002 OBU Connections (2), CORE 1023 The Contemporary World (3), CORE 1043 Composition I (3), CORE 1113 Survey of the Bible (3), CORE 1123 Interpreting the Bible (3), CORE 2233 World Literature (3), CORE 2243 History of World Societies (3), CORE 2334 Scientific Inquiry (4), CORE 3023 Scientific Connections (3). Total Credit Hours for Common Core: 27. Note: Entering freshmen must enroll in OBU Connections within their first two semesters at Ouachita, and until they have successfully completed the course, they must continue to enroll in it each semester thereafter. This requirement is waived for transfer students who have been enrolled full-time for two semesters at another college or university. FLEXIBLE CORE (Students may choose from courses listed below to satisfy each menu.): Analytic and Quantitative Reasoning (Choose one course*) 3 - MATH 1003 College Algebra; MATH 1033 Mathematics for the Liberal Arts; PHIL 1003 Introduction to Philosophy; PHIL 1023 Logic. *Students with an MPI less than 80 must choose one of the MATH courses in this menu. Applied Skills (Choose one course) 3 - COMM 1003 Fundamentals of Public Speaking; FINN 2003 Personal Finance. Artistic Engagement (Choose one course**) 3 - FINA 3113 Fine Arts: Art; FINA 3123 Fine Arts: Music; FINA 3133 Fine Arts: Theatre. **Upon approval by the Dean of Interdisciplinary Studies, participation in the European Study Program earns 3 hours of generic Fine Arts credit. Civic Engagement in America (Choose one course) 3 - HIST 2003 United States History to 1877; HIST 2013 United States History Since 1877; PSCI 2013 American National Government. Inter…

items.label: Analytic and Quantitative Reasoning (Choose one course)
items.note: Students with an MPI less than 80 must choose one of the MATH courses in this menu.

items.label: Artistic Engagement (Choose one course)
items.note: Upon approval by the Dean of Interdisciplinary Studies, participation in the European Study Program earns 3 hours of generic Fine Arts credit.

items.label: Civic Engagement in America (Choose one course)
Intercultural Appreciation and Communication
items.text: The equivalent of two semesters of credit must be earned in the study of a language other than English, taken in sequence from a lower to higher level of competency. Students may not earn credit for a lower-level course in a language for which they have already earned credit at a more advanced level. Languages offered at Ouachita include Chinese (CHIN), French (FREN), German (GERM), Greek (GREK), Hebrew (HEBR), Italian (ITAL), Japanese (JAPN), Latin (LATN), and Spanish (SPAN). This menu may also be satisfied by an approved language-intensive, study-abroad experience in a non-English-speaking country. The menu is waived for international students.

items.label: Physical Well-being (one course)
items.note: KIN 1002 is 2 hours; KIN 2073 and KIN 2013 are 3 hours, so this menu is 2-3 hours.

items.label: Chapel
items.text: CHAP 1000 Chapel (7 chapel credits required). A student must earn a chapel credit for every full-time semester (minimum of 12 semester hours) enrolled at Ouachita, up to a maximum of 7 credits.

items.label: Arts Engagement Series (attendance)
items.text: Students must attend three approved events (one each in visual art, music, and theatre) for each year of full-time enrollment in a residential degree program, up to a maximum of 12 required events.

notes: Common Core courses are required of all students, though in limited cases, introductory courses in the major may substitute for some required courses (see major requirements).

Entering freshmen must enroll in CORE 1002 OBU Connections within their first two semesters and must continue to enroll in it each semester thereafter until they have successfully completed it; waived for transfer students who have been enrolled full-time for two semesters at another college or university.
Students with an MPI less than 80 must choose one of the MATH courses in the Analytic and Quantitative Reasoning menu.

FINA 3113/3123/3133 (Artistic Engagement menu) are open to students with junior standing (59+ hours) and to sophomores (29+ hours) who are currently up to date with the attendance requirement for the Arts Engagement Series, normally six arts events; exceptions may be made individually for students with special circumstances.

Chapel: one chapel credit for every full-time semester (minimum 12 semester hours) enrolled, up to a maximum of 7 credits; to receive a semester's credit a student must attend at least three-fourths of the scheduled chapel programs (no more than 4 misses).

Arts Engagement Series attendance is verified by a swipe card system; students who fall behind may make up deficiencies by attending extra events in a later year; the requirement may not be satisfied by taking additional Fine Arts courses, nor by attending off-campus events except those in an approved university-sponsored semester study program.

FINA 4011 is open to seniors only, graded Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory, has no regular class meeting, and requires completion of the Arts Engagement Series attendance requirements plus an online reflection survey.

Writing Program: College Writing 1 = CORE 1043 Composition I or equivalent; College Writing 2 = an approved writing course in the major, an approved writing course in the English Department, or CORE 2053 Composition II; College Writing 3 = an approved upper-level course in the major. Courses satisfying CW2/CW3 are tagged [CW2]/[CW3].

Oral Communication Program: all students must have an oral intensive experience including instruction in public speaking, multiple presentations, and feedback, designed by departmental faculty within each major.
Senior Capstone: each student must complete a capstone course designed by faculty as part of the requirements for a major or school.
The catalog prints a total of 48-49 credit hours for the Ouachita Core (Common 27, Flexible 20-21, Experiential 1).
extraction_notes: stated_hours is null because the catalog prints a range (48-49) rather than a single number.
The three-part structure is represented as three top-level 'all' nodes: Common Core, Flexible Core, Experiential Core.

Intercultural Appreciation and Communication is a manual node: the catalog states a sequenced two-semester language requirement (or an approved language-intensive study-abroad substitute, or a waiver for international students) rather than a fixed course list.
Physical Well-being is a choose(count 1) node; its total is 2-3 hours, which is why the Flexible Core total is printed as 20-21.

CORE 2053 Composition II is NOT part of the printed Common Core list; it is an option for the College Writing 2 requirement, so it is not included in the Common Core node (the course record still exists).
Chapel (7 credits) and the Arts Engagement Series attendance (up to 12 events) are manual (non-course) requirements.
Menus in this catalog carry no '(Satisfied by ...)' substitution clauses; the printed asterisk notes were placed in the node 'note' fields and in notes.

programs.name: Accounting
programs.school: Frank D. Hickingbotham School of Business
programs.source_text: A major in accounting requires completion of the University Core, the Basic School Requirements, the Business Core, and the course work designated for the chosen major. Additionally, accounting majors must earn a 2.000 GPA in the major and have at least 24 hours of "C" or higher in the major. ACCOUNTING MAJOR 37 Hours: ACCT 2013 Principles of Accounting I; ACCT 2023 Principles of Accounting II; ACCT 2033 Data Analytics for Accounting and Finance; ACCT 3014 Intermediate Accounting I; ACCT 3023 Intermediate Accounting II; ACCT 3033 Cost Accounting; ACCT 3053 Institutional Accounting; ACCT 3073 Accounting Information Systems; ACCT 4003 Federal Income Tax; ACCT 4013 Advanced Accounting; ACCT 4023 Principles and Procedures of Auditing; ACCT 4113 Accounting Perspectives: An Integrative Capstone. Each student who earns a Bachelor of Arts in the School of Business will meet the University residence and chapel requirements, successfully complete the courses associated with the chosen major, achieve an overall GPA of 2.000, achieve a 2.000 GPA at Ouachita and earn at least 120 hours. At least one half of the total hours in business must be taken at Ouachita, and each student must earn at least 39 hours from the 3000/4000 level. At least 60 of the 120 hours must be earned at Ouachita.

items.label: Economics (six hours, three at Junior-Senior level)

notes: No minor is required in the School of Business.

Each student must earn at least 39 hours from the 3000/4000 level; at least one half of the total business hours must be taken at Ouachita; at least 60 of the 120 hours must be earned at Ouachita (half of the total).

programs.name: Biblical Languages
programs.school: Chesley and Elizabeth Pruet School of Christian Studies
programs.source_text: A Major in Biblical Languages requires the completion of the University CORE, 30 hours of GREK and HEBR courses, a minor in Christian Studies (see above), CHST 1001, CHST 4601, PHIL 4013, and an Internship/Service Component. Students may choose to major in Christian Studies in place of the minor. This major equips students to read and interpret biblical texts directly from the language in which they were originally written.

requirements.label: Minor in Christian Studies (or a major in Christian Studies in place of the minor)
requirements.text: A minor in Christian Studies is required; students may choose to major in Christian Studies in place of the minor.

requirements.label: Internship/Service Component
requirements.text: Fulfillment of the Internship/Service Component is achieved by one of the following: 1. Tuition Credit Internship: Regular internship course offerings are available to be taken during a regular semester or the summer term. These can be 1-3 hours of academic credit and will serve as part of the student's academic load for the semester taken. Credit internships must be preapproved by submitting the proper paperwork to the appropriate Internship Supervisor. Guidelines and forms are available in the Dean's Office. 2. Non-credit Internship: An internship in an approved ministry may fulfill this requirement. It must entail a minimum of 50 hours of ministry. Non-credit internships must be preapproved by submitting the proper paperwork to the appropriate Internship Supervisor. Guidelines and forms are available in the Dean's Office. 3. Completing one semester of TranServe (minimum 20 hours) through the Elrod Center. 4. Completing the Supervised Hospital Ministry course (CHMM 4406) or the Church Planting Practicum course (CHMM 4843) 5. Successful participation in the CHMM 3073 Christian Missions Study Trip.

notes: Requires a minor in Christian Studies; a major in Christian Studies may be substituted for that minor.
Requires the completion of the University CORE and an Internship/Service Component.
All majors in the School of Christian Studies, except the Major in Christian Foundations, require an Internship/Service Component.

programs.source_text:
A Co-major in Christian Foundations requires completion of the University Core and a major outside of the School of Christian Studies. This major serves as a co-major for students pursuing a primary major in a discipline outside of Christian Studies. It may not be paired with another major in Christian Studies except for the traditional major in Philosophy or major in Community & Family Services with a minor or additional major. This major provides a foundation for students interested in the Christian faith and practice of ministry but whose primary major makes a major in Christian Studies unmanageable. An internship component is not required for this major.

programs.name: Christian Studies
programs.school: Chesley and Elizabeth Pruet School of Christian Studies
programs.source_text:
Major in Christian Studies (with an emphasis in Biblical Studies & Theology, Christian Ministry & Missions, Philosophy, or an Interdisciplinary emphasis).

A Major in Christian Studies prepares students to follow the Lord as faithful disciples, to produce valid interpretations and appropriate applications of the Bible, to share a faithful and loving gospel witness, to engage the contemporary world in light of Scripture and the history of Christian thought, and to serve with competency and spiritual maturity in a ministry setting.

The major requires the completion of the University Core and an Internship/Service Component. No minor is required.

1. Christian Studies Basic Requirements (35 hours)
CHST 1001 Freshman Seminar
BSTH 1003 Spiritual Formation
PHIL 1003 Introduction to Philosophy
BSTH 2023 Biblical Exegesis
BSTH 2403 Foundational Christian Theology
CHMM 2003 The Church and Ministry
CHMM 2303 The Christian Mission
BSTH 3323 History of Christianity
CHMM 3403 World Religions
____ ___3 Three hours of Jr/Sr-level OT or NT elective from BSTH or Jr/Sr-level course from GREK or HEBR
One of the following:
  CHMM 4203 Teaching to Change Lives
  CHMM 4213 Preaching the Bible
PHIL 4013 Christian Ethics
CHST 4601 Senior Seminar
2. Christian Studies Emphasis (9 hours): Students must take nine hours of emphasis electives in one of the three departments (BSTH, CHMM, or PHIL) for a departmental emphasis, or nine assorted hours in BSTH, CHMM, or PHIL for an Interdisciplinary Emphasis.
3. Internship/Service Component

All majors in the School of Christian Studies, except the Major in Christian Foundations, require an Internship/Service Component. Fulfillment of the Internship/Service Component is achieved by one of the following: 1. Tuition Credit Internship: Regular internship course offerings are available to be taken during a regular semester or the summer term. These can be 1-3 hours of academic credit and will serve as part of the student's academic load for the semester…

items.label: Three hours of Jr/Sr-level OT or NT elective from BSTH or Jr/Sr-level course from GREK or HEBR

requirements.label: Christian Studies emphasis electives (9 hours, Biblical Studies & Theology)
Internship/Service Component
requirements.text: Fulfillment of the Internship/Service Component is achieved by one of the following: 1. Tuition Credit Internship: Regular internship course offerings are available to be taken during a regular semester or the summer term. These can be 1-3 hours of academic credit and will serve as part of the student's academic load for the semester taken. Credit internships must be preapproved by submitting the proper paperwork to the appropriate Internship Supervisor. Guidelines and forms are available in the Dean's Office. 2. Non-credit Internship: An internship in an approved ministry may fulfill this requirement. It must entail a minimum of 50 hours of ministry. Non-credit internships must be preapproved by submitting the proper paperwork to the appropriate Internship Supervisor. Guidelines and forms are available in the Dean's Office. 3. Completing one semester of TranServe (minimum 20 hours) through the Elrod Center. 4. Completing the Supervised Hospital Ministry course (CHMM 4406) or the Church Planting Practicum course (CHMM 4843) 5. Successful participation in the CHMM 3073 Christian Missions Study Trip.

programs.source_text:
A Major in Philosophy requires the completion of the University Core, the following requirements in the School of Christian Studies (total of 28 hours), and an Internship/Service Component. A minor is required for a traditional Philosophy major.

PHIL 1003 Introduction to Philosophy
PHIL 1023 Logic
BSTH 2403 Foundational Christian Theology
One of the following:
  PHIL 3003 Ancient and Medieval Philosophy
  PHIL 4003 Modern and Contemporary Philosophy
PHIL ___3 Philosophy elective
PHIL ___3 Philosophy elective
PHIL ¾__3 Upper-level Philosophy elective
PHIL ¾__3 Upper-level Philosophy elective
PHIL 4013 Christian Ethics

requirements.label: Philosophy requirements in the School of Christian Studies (28 hours)
Internship/Service Component
requirements.text: Fulfillment of the Internship/Service Component is achieved by one of the following: 1. Tuition Credit Internship: Regular internship course offerings are available to be taken during a regular semester or the summer term. These can be 1-3 hours of academic credit and will serve as part of the student's academic load for the semester taken. Credit internships must be preapproved by submitting the proper paperwork to the appropriate Internship Supervisor. Guidelines and forms are available in the Dean's Office. 2. Non-credit Internship: An internship in an approved ministry may fulfill this requirement. It must entail a minimum of 50 hours of ministry. Non-credit internships must be preapproved by submitting the proper paperwork to the appropriate Internship Supervisor. Guidelines and forms are available in the Dean's Office. 3. Completing one semester of TranServe (minimum 20 hours) through the Elrod Center. 4. Completing the Supervised Hospital Ministry course (CHMM 4406) or the Church Planting Practicum course (CHMM 4843) 5. Successful participation in the CHMM 3073 Christian Missions Study Trip.

notes: A minor is required for a traditional Philosophy major.
Requires the completion of the University Core and an Internship/Service Component.
All majors in the School of Christian Studies, except the Major in Christian Foundations, require an Internship/Service Component.
extraction_notes: stated_hours 28 is the total of the School of Christian Studies requirements as printed; the University Core and the internship are outside that 28 hours.

Ouachita's Education Studies Minor (20 hours, including 6 Jr./Sr. hours), which may be taken with any major, is designed to provide a greater understanding of the teaching field in general as well as specific information regarding such areas as teaching strategies, classroom management, and student diversity. programs.name: International Studies
programs.department: Daniel and Betty Jo Grant Center for International Education
programs.source_text: International Studies Minor. A minor in International Studies will include at least 27 hours as follows: 1. Language Component: The student must complete two years of study in one foreign language for a total of 12 to 14 hours. At least one semester of the language must be taken prior to the overseas study experience. The language study must be in a field relevant to the overseas study experience. 2. Overseas Study: The student must complete at least one semester of overseas study experience in a program approved in advance by the director of international education. 3. International Studies Seminar: The student must complete this one-hour seminar, INTL 4001, after returning from the overseas study experience. 4. Additional Requirements: The student must complete other approved courses to fulfill the 27-hour minor. These may include pre-approved courses taken overseas or on-campus courses related to the student's degree program. Such courses will include, but are not necessarily limited to: PSCI 3013, World Politics; PSCI 4023, Comparative Politics; HIST 4703-4793, Topical Seminar (only as approved); CHMM 3403, World Religions; CHMM / COMM 4313, Intercultural Communication; BUAD 3103, Global Business. Other courses must be approved by the director of international education. The student must achieve at least a 2.000 GPA on all course work included in the minor.

programs.name: Military Science
programs.source_text: Requirements for a Minor in Military Science: A minor in Military Science requires completion of the university CORE, a university recognized major, and 19 hours of the following MSCI courses: MSCI 2032, 2042, 3053, 3063, 3093, 4073 and 4083. In addition, a non-credit leadership lab is required in conjunction with other MSCI courses. The Military Science minor recognizes the efforts of Military Science students in completion of the 19 hours of Military Science that are required to become a 2nd Lieutenant in the U.S. Army. The University recognizes the past, present, and future work and dedication of the students that meet the requirements for the Military Science minor.
notes: The minor requires completion of the university CORE and a university recognized major in addition to the 19 MSCI hours.
The 19 hours of Military Science are those required to become a 2nd Lieutenant in the U.S. Army.

The listed courses are the advanced course sequence; most are restricted to ROTC contracted students (the advanced-course heading reads 'Military Science Advanced Courses (Junior, Seniors—Only ROTC Contracted Students)').
extraction_notes: The catalog phrase 'a non-credit leadership lab is required in conjunction with other MSCI courses' does not name a course code; it is resolved to MSCI 1000 Leadership Lab, the only leadership lab in the MSCI course list, and represented as a 0-hour course node.
MSCI 3093 has no stated offering term in the catalog (see courses.json notes); it is required for the minor regardless.
The minor's course list is complete (2032+2042+3053+3063+3093+4073+4083 = 19 hours), so an 'all' node is used rather than a choose/hours node.
